concepts.title: Acceleration
concepts.description: The instantaneous rate of change of velocity with respect to time in a specified reference frame. It can result from changing speed, changing direction, or both.

concepts.title: Action Functional
concepts.description: A functional assigning an action value to a trajectory; in first-order mechanics S[q] is the time integral of L(q, qdot, t) over a specified interval.

relations.note: The input is an entire candidate trajectory.
The mechanical action integrates a Lagrangian.
The introductory smooth mechanical action is a definite time integral over a finite interval.
Physical trajectories are characterized by stationarity, not necessarily minimization, of action.

concepts.title: Adiabatic Process
concepts.description: A thermodynamic process with no heat transfer across the system boundary throughout the process; work or, for an open system, matter can still transfer energy.

relations.note: Adiabaticity excludes heat transfer throughout the process.
Two reversible adiabatic stages connect the hot and cold isotherms.

concepts.title: Adiabatic Theorem
concepts.description: A result that sufficiently slow, smooth Hamiltonian variation keeps an initially isolated energy eigenstate close to its corresponding instantaneous eigenspace.

concepts.title: Affine Connection
concepts.description: A rule for covariantly differentiating vector fields on a smooth manifold, enabling comparison of tangent vectors along directions and curves.

concepts.title: Affine Parameter
concepts.description: A parameter along a geodesic for which its tangent parallel-transports itself, determined up to λ ↦ aλ + b with nonzero constant a.

relations.note: Null geodesics admit affine parameters even though proper time cannot parametrize them.

concepts.title: Angular Momentum
concepts.description: In classical particle mechanics, the moment of linear momentum about a specified point, summed over the system. Its evolution is governed by torque under the appropriate reference-point and interaction assumptions; it is not generally parallel to angular velocity.

relations.note: In oriented three-dimensional Euclidean space, a particle's orbital angular momentum is position crossed with linear momentum.
A force directed toward a fixed center produces zero torque about that center.

concepts.title: Angular Velocity
concepts.description: An axial vector specifying the instantaneous rate and oriented axis of rotation relative to a chosen reference frame. A rigid body has one angular velocity shared by all its material points; finite orientation changes are not ordinary vectors.

relations.note: In oriented three-dimensional Euclidean space, the cross product relates angular velocity to a rigid body's point velocities.

concepts.title: Antiparticle
concepts.description: A particle's conjugate partner, with the same mass and spin but opposite additive charges; some neutral particles are their own antiparticles.

concepts.title: Atomic Orbital
concepts.description: A one-electron spatial wavefunction associated with an atom. Its squared magnitude determines a position probability density; orbital descriptions of many-electron atoms use an appropriate one-electron approximation.

relations.note: An orbital is a spatial wavefunction rather than a particle path.

concepts.title: Atomic Physics
concepts.description: The study of atomic electronic structure, transitions between atomic states, and interactions of atoms and ions with radiation and external fields.

relations.note: Quantum theory supplies the modern description of atomic states and transitions.

concepts.title: Azimuthal Quantum Number
concepts.description: The nonnegative integer ell that labels an atomic orbital's angular momentum magnitude and subshell. The familiar s, p, d and f subshells have ell equal to 0, 1, 2 and 3.

relations.note: Ell specifies an eigenvalue of the squared orbital angular momentum operator.
Ell labels the orbital's angular factor and subshell.

concepts.title: Basis
concepts.description: A linearly independent spanning set of a vector space, so that every vector has a unique finite linear-combination expansion in its elements; this record uses the algebraic basis convention.

relations.note: Chosen bases specify coordinates and the matrix of a finite-dimensional linear map.

concepts.title: Bernoulli Principle
concepts.description: For steady inviscid flow of constant density under gravity, the sum of pressure, kinetic-energy density and gravitational potential-energy density is constant along a streamline.

concepts.title: Black-Body Radiation
concepts.description: Equilibrium thermal electromagnetic radiation with a spectrum fixed by temperature, realized ideally in a cavity or emitted by a perfect absorber.

relations.note: Absolute temperature specifies the equilibrium black-body spectrum.

concepts.title: Bloch Sphere
concepts.description: A geometric representation of pure two-state-system states as points on a sphere; mixed states occupy its interior in the Bloch-ball extension.

concepts.title: Bloch's Theorem
concepts.description: For a Hamiltonian with lattice-translation symmetry, an energy eigenbasis can be chosen as plane waves multiplied by functions with the lattice periodicity.

relations.note: Bloch's theorem organizes stationary Schrödinger eigenstates in a periodic potential.
Bloch wavevectors and band indices label electron energies in a periodic crystal.

concepts.title: Bohr Model
concepts.description: A historical atomic model that combines Coulomb-bound circular electron orbits with discrete angular momentum and radiative transitions. It reproduces the leading hydrogenic energy spectrum but does not give the modern orbital description.

relations.note: Coulomb attraction provides the model's centripetal force.
The historical quantization postulate constrains the classical circular-orbit angular momentum.

concepts.title: Boltzmann Distribution
concepts.description: The equilibrium probability law assigning each microscopic state a normalized weight proportional to the exponential of minus its energy divided by Boltzmann's constant times temperature.

concepts.title: Boltzmann Entropy
concepts.description: An entropy S = kB ln Ω assigned to a macrostate, where Ω counts compatible microscopic states or a dimensionless coarse-grained phase-space volume.

relations.note: The multiplicity is relative to specified macroscopic constraints.
Equilibrium multiplicities provide a statistical interpretation of thermodynamic entropy.

concepts.title: Born Approximation
concepts.description: A weak-scattering approximation that replaces the interacting wave inside the scattering integral by the incident wave, giving the first perturbative scattering amplitude.

relations.note: The approximation estimates the outgoing scattering amplitude.
The first Born amplitude is proportional to the spatial Fourier transform of the potential.

concepts.title: Born Rule
concepts.description: The quantum probability rule assigning Tr(rho P) to a projective measurement event P in state rho, reducing to the squared projected amplitude for a normalized pure state.

relations.note: Projective measurements of sharp observables provide the introductory case.

concepts.title: Bose–Einstein Condensate
concepts.description: A state of bosonic matter characterized by macroscopic occupation of a single-particle quantum state, with the ideal Bose gas providing an introductory equilibrium model.

relations.note: The ideal-gas condensation mechanism follows from bosonic occupation statistics.

concepts.title: Bose–Einstein Statistics
concepts.description: Quantum statistics for identical bosons, allowing any nonnegative occupation of a single-particle state; for noninteracting particles it yields the Bose–Einstein occupation distribution.

relations.note: Bosonic exchange symmetry permits unrestricted nonnegative occupation of each state.
For conserved particles, the chemical potential fixes the mean population.
The independent-state grand-canonical geometric sum gives the bosonic mean occupation.

concepts.title: Bose Gas
concepts.description: An ideal many-particle model of noninteracting identical bosons, with equilibrium state populations governed by Bose–Einstein statistics.

relations.note: Bose–Einstein statistics governs the equilibrium populations of the ideal model.
The ideal Bose gas supplies a baseline model of condensation.

concepts.title: Boson
concepts.description: A particle with integer spin whose identical-particle quantum states are symmetric under exchange, allowing multiple particles in one state in ordinary three-dimensional physics.

relations.note: Integer intrinsic spin characterizes bosons in the ordinary spin-statistics setting.
Bose–Einstein state counting applies to identical bosons.

concepts.title: Bound State
concepts.description: A normalizable quantum state confined by an interaction or boundary conditions; stationary bound states are normalizable energy eigenstates.

relations.note: Spatial normalizability distinguishes the scoped bound-state solutions.
Stationary bound-state energies solve the Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem.

concepts.title: Brillouin Zone
concepts.description: A reciprocal-space region used to organize waves in a crystal; the first Brillouin zone is the Wigner–Seitz cell of the reciprocal lattice.

relations.note: Restricting Bloch wavevectors to one first zone avoids reciprocal-lattice-equivalent labels in the reduced-zone band description.

concepts.title: Buoyancy
concepts.description: The resultant upward force exerted by hydrostatic fluid pressure on an immersed body; its magnitude equals the weight of the displaced fluid under Archimedes' conditions.

concepts.title: Calculus
concepts.description: The mathematical study of continuous change and accumulation through derivatives, integrals, limits, and related constructions used throughout theoretical physics.

relations.note: Differential and integral techniques support physical models.

concepts.title: Canonical Ensemble
concepts.description: An equilibrium ensemble at fixed temperature, volume, and particle number, with microscopic probabilities proportional to exp(−E/kBT) and energy allowed to fluctuate.

relations.note: It specifies an equilibrium probability distribution.
Temperature is fixed by a thermal reservoir.
Its normalization defines the canonical partition function.

concepts.title: Canonical Quantization
concepts.description: An approach that promotes selected classical canonical variables to quantum operators with canonical commutation or graded relations, requiring care with ordering, domains, and constraints rather than a unique quantization of every observable.

concepts.title: Canonical Transformation
concepts.description: A smooth, locally invertible transformation of canonical phase-space coordinates that preserves their Poisson-bracket structure. Time-dependent transformations are allowed, with the Hamiltonian transformed accordingly.

relations.note: Canonical changes of phase-space coordinates preserve the Liouville volume used in classical phase-space ensemble integrals.
A generating function can construct canonical coordinates in which the transformed Hamiltonian vanishes; the resulting condition is the Hamilton–Jacobi equation.

concepts.title: Carnot Cycle
concepts.description: An ideal reversible cycle composed of two isothermal heat-exchange stages and two adiabatic stages, setting the maximum heat-engine efficiency between two reservoirs.

relations.note: Reversible isothermal stages provide heat exchange at each reservoir temperature.
Reversible adiabatic stages connect the two isotherms without heat transfer.
The reversible cycle supplies the maximum efficiency for engines using the same two reservoirs.

concepts.title: Cauchy Stress
concepts.description: The second-order tensor that determines contact force per unit current area on an oriented surface through a point in a continuum, including normal and shear components.

concepts.title: Causal Character of Vectors
concepts.description: For a Lorentzian metric, a nonzero tangent vector is timelike, null or spacelike according to its metric norm and the chosen signature convention.

relations.note: Along a Levi-Civita geodesic in Lorentzian geometry the causal character of its tangent is preserved.

concepts.title: Center of Mass
concepts.description: The mass-weighted mean position of a material system. For a fixed Newtonian particle system whose internal forces cancel, its translational acceleration is determined by total external force divided by total mass.

relations.note: The center-of-mass coordinate separates collective translation from internal motion.

concepts.title: Central-Force Motion
concepts.description: Classical particle motion under a force directed along the separation from a fixed center and depending only on that separation. Angular momentum is conserved; for nonzero angular momentum the trajectory lies in a fixed plane, and radial motion admits an effective-potential description.

relations.note: Attractive inverse-square forces give the Kepler special case of central-force motion.

concepts.title: Chemical Potential
concepts.description: The thermodynamic energy variable conjugate to the amount of a species, quantifying how the appropriate thermodynamic potential changes when particles are added under specified constraints.

relations.note: Chemical potential is the derivative of internal energy with respect to particle number at fixed entropy and volume.
The reservoir chemical potential controls particle exchange in a grand-canonical ensemble.

concepts.title: Christoffel Symbol
concepts.description: The coefficients of the Levi-Civita connection in a coordinate basis, computed from a metric and its first derivatives in the scope used here.

relations.note: The Levi-Civita Christoffel symbols are computed from the metric and its first derivatives.
They appear in the coordinate form of the geodesic equation.
In the Levi-Civita case they enter the coordinate expression for the Riemann curvature tensor.
Levi-Civita coefficients supply the connection terms for metric geodesics.
Levi-Civita coefficients enter the coordinate expressions for spacetime covariant derivatives, geodesics and curvature.

concepts.title: Chromatic Dispersion
concepts.description: Frequency dependence of light's phase speed in a medium, equivalently frequency dependence of its refractive index. It can make different spectral components refract by different amounts.

relations.note: The material dispersion is expressed by the variation of phase index with frequency.
Using the index at each frequency explains wavelength-dependent ray refraction in a prism.

concepts.title: Classical Field
concepts.description: A non-quantum assignment of scalar values or geometric quantities to points of space or spacetime, providing continuously distributed degrees of freedom rather than quantum operators.

relations.note: Scalar fields are one class of classical field.
The classical electromagnetic field is a particular tensor-valued field.

concepts.title: Classical Field Theory
concepts.description: The study of non-quantum fields with degrees of freedom distributed over space or spacetime, including their equations of motion, symmetries, and conservation laws.

relations.note: This introductory route emphasizes action-based field theories.

concepts.title: Classical Mechanics
concepts.description: The non-quantum study of motion and interactions, including particle, rigid-body, and continuum systems, using Newtonian, Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, and other formulations.

relations.note: Continuous-time mechanical dynamics uses differentiation and integration.

concepts.title: Classical Scalar Field
concepts.description: A real- or complex-valued classical field whose value at a spacetime event is unchanged by a coordinate transformation, although the coordinates labeling that event change.

relations.note: Scalar-field models provide a simple setting for local action dynamics.

concepts.title: Clifford Algebra
concepts.description: A unital associative algebra generated by a vector space with a quadratic form, subject to the relation v² = Q(v)1; the associated symmetric bilinear form fixes the anticommutator of generating vectors.

relations.note: The generators are drawn from a vector space equipped with a quadratic form.
Clifford modules provide spinor representations.
Pauli matrices realize the three-dimensional Euclidean Clifford relations used for spin one-half.
Gamma-matrix Clifford relations support relativistic spinor field equations.

concepts.title: Closed Form
concepts.description: A differential form omega satisfying d omega = 0. Closedness does not, on a general manifold, imply the existence of a globally defined form whose exterior derivative is omega.

relations.note: Every exact form is closed because d squared is zero; the converse need not hold globally.

concepts.title: Commutator
concepts.description: In the operator and associative-algebra scope used here, the operation [A,B] = AB − BA measures the failure of multiplication or operator composition to commute.

relations.note: The operator specialization compares the two orders of composition on a common domain.
Hamiltonian commutators generate Heisenberg operator evolution.
The Robertson uncertainty bound contains the expectation of an observable commutator.

concepts.title: Complex Manifold
concepts.description: A Hausdorff, second-countable space with local complex coordinates whose overlap transitions are biholomorphic, determining an underlying smooth manifold of even real dimension.

concepts.title: Configuration Space
concepts.description: The space of allowed instantaneous positions and orientations of a mechanical system, excluding velocities and momenta.

relations.note: A mechanical trajectory is a path through configuration space.
Configuration variables form part of the Hamiltonian description.

concepts.title: Connection Coefficients
concepts.description: Local functions expressing covariant derivatives of basis vector fields in a chosen frame; they do not transform as components of a tensor.

relations.note: The Core Christoffel concept is restricted to Levi-Civita coefficients in a coordinate basis.

concepts.title: Connection Transformation Law
concepts.description: The coordinate-change rule for connection coefficients includes second derivatives of the coordinate transformation, explaining why Christoffel symbols are not tensor components.

concepts.title: Conservation of Linear Momentum
concepts.description: Constancy of a system's total linear momentum when there is no net external force. For a fixed Newtonian particle system, the standard derivation assumes that the internal forces cancel in the total momentum balance.

relations.note: The conservation condition distinguishes cancelling internal forces from the net external force.
Summing particle momentum balances yields conservation when internal forces cancel and the net external force vanishes.

concepts.title: Conservative Force
concepts.description: A position-dependent force whose work between any two points in its domain is independent of the connecting path. Under suitable regularity this is equivalent to a single-valued potential energy with force equal to its negative gradient.

concepts.title: Continuity
concepts.description: The property that a function's values approach its value at a point as inputs approach that point within its domain; continuity on a domain requires this at every point.

concepts.title: Continuum Mechanics
concepts.description: Mechanics of matter modeled as a continuous distribution, using fields for motion, internal forces and material response at scales where molecular discreteness can be averaged.

relations.note: The classical force-balance formulation uses Newton's law for material portions.

concepts.title: Coordinate Basis
concepts.description: The local tangent basis formed by coordinate derivatives ∂/∂x^a; its basis vector fields commute, unlike a general noncoordinate frame.

concepts.title: Coordinate Chart
concepts.description: A homeomorphism from an open region of a manifold onto an open region of Euclidean space, assigning local coordinates to its points.

relations.note: Compatible charts form an atlas.

concepts.title: Cosmic Microwave Background
concepts.description: Relic electromagnetic radiation from the early hot universe, observed today with an almost thermal microwave spectrum and small anisotropies.

relations.note: Its nearly thermal spectrum is described using black-body radiation.
Expansion shifts the relic spectrum toward lower photon energies.
The spectrum and anisotropies test cosmological models.

concepts.title: Cosmological Constant
concepts.description: A constant term proportional to the metric in Einstein’s field equations, equivalently represented as a uniform vacuum-energy stress tensor.

relations.note: The constant multiplies the metric in the gravitational field equations.
A cosmological constant contributes to homogeneous expansion and acceleration.

concepts.title: Cosmological Principle
concepts.description: The modeling assumption that the universe is statistically homogeneous and isotropic on sufficiently large spatial scales.

relations.note: Homogeneous and isotropic spatial slices motivate the FLRW family of background metrics.

concepts.title: Cosmological Redshift
concepts.description: The change in photon wavelength associated with propagation through an evolving cosmological background between comoving emitters and observers.

relations.note: The background wavelength ratio equals the relative change in scale factor.
Cosmic expansion redshifts the relic photon spectrum.

concepts.title: Physical Cosmology
concepts.description: The physical study of the universe’s large-scale structure, contents, origin, and evolution, tested against astronomical observations.

concepts.title: Cotangent Space
concepts.description: The linear dual of a tangent space, consisting of covectors that map tangent vectors at a point of a smooth manifold to scalars.

relations.note: The cotangent space is obtained as the linear dual of the tangent space at the same point.
Covectors are scalar-valued linear maps on the tangent space.

concepts.title: Coulomb’s Law
concepts.description: The inverse-square electrostatic force law for two stationary point charges in vacuum.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped coulomb’s law formulation.
Needed for the scoped coulomb’s law formulation.
Needed for the scoped coulomb’s law formulation.

concepts.title: Creation and Annihilation Operators
concepts.description: Operators that raise or lower occupation in specified particle modes, with bosonic commutation or fermionic anticommutation relations and the appropriate normalization on Fock states.

relations.note: Free-field mode expansions are expressed through creation and annihilation operators.

concepts.title: Critical Phenomena
concepts.description: Collective behavior near continuous phase transitions, where long-range correlations and fluctuations can produce singular responses and universal scaling.

relations.note: Criticality concerns the neighborhood of suitable continuous phase transitions.
True divergent correlation lengths refer to the thermodynamic limit.
The Ising model supplies benchmark examples of critical behavior.

concepts.title: Cross Product
concepts.description: An order-sensitive product of two vectors in oriented three-dimensional Euclidean space. Its result is perpendicular to both inputs, with length equal to the area of the parallelogram they span. The chosen orientation fixes its sign through the right-hand rule. Parallel inputs, or a zero input, give the zero vector.

relations.note: Uses three-dimensional vector components, lengths, and directions.

concepts.title: Curl
concepts.description: The differential operator measuring local circulation of a vector field in oriented three-dimensional Euclidean space.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped curl formulation.
Needed for the scoped curl formulation.
Needed for the scoped curl formulation.

concepts.title: Curvature Singularity
concepts.description: A genuine breakdown signaled by unbounded curvature, such as the divergence of curvature invariants at r = 0 in Schwarzschild; not every spacetime singularity is of this type.

relations.note: For positive Schwarzschild mass, r = 0 is a curvature singularity; r = 2GM/c² is not.

concepts.title: Cyclic Coordinate
concepts.description: A generalized coordinate on which the chosen Lagrangian has no explicit dependence, so its conjugate momentum is conserved along Euler-Lagrange solutions.

relations.note: The conserved quantity is the coordinate's conjugate momentum.
The conservation statement follows from the Euler-Lagrange equation.

concepts.title: Damped Harmonic Oscillator
concepts.description: The linear oscillator family with a restoring force and nonnegative velocity-proportional damping, including the zero-damping limit. It contains underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped regimes; the latter two do not exhibit sustained back-and-forth motion.

relations.note: The model family includes zero damping, which recovers the undamped harmonic oscillator.
Combine a linear restoring force with a force proportional and opposite to velocity.

concepts.title: de Rham Cohomology
concepts.description: The cohomology of the complex of smooth differential forms, whose positive-degree groups are closed forms modulo exact forms and whose degree-zero group consists of locally constant functions.

concepts.title: Density Matrix
concepts.description: An operator representation of a quantum state formed from pure-state projectors with nonnegative statistical weights summing to one, representing both pure and mixed states and their measurement statistics.

relations.note: Statistical mixtures are represented by weighted sums of pure-state projectors.

concepts.title: Density of States
concepts.description: The number of available physical modes or quantum states per energy interval for a specified system, independent of how those states are occupied.

relations.note: Combining the density of states with Fermi–Dirac occupations gives particle number and energy.
Energy-state counting weights the Bose occupation integrals.

concepts.title: Derivative
concepts.description: For a real-valued function of one real variable, the limit of its difference quotient at a point when that finite limit exists, measuring the function's local rate of change.

relations.note: The equation differentiates a state with respect to time.

concepts.title: Diffeomorphism
concepts.description: An invertible smooth map between smooth manifolds with a smooth inverse, expressing equivalence of their smooth structures.

relations.note: Overlap transitions are Euclidean diffeomorphisms.

concepts.title: Differential Form
concepts.description: A smooth covariant tensor field of degree k that is alternating in its tangent-vector arguments. Differential forms provide a coordinate-independent language for integration on smooth manifolds.

relations.note: Closed forms satisfy the additional condition that their exterior derivative vanishes.

concepts.title: Differential Geometry
concepts.description: The study of smooth manifolds and geometric structures using differential calculus, providing the language for curvature, connections, and relativistic spacetime.

concepts.title: Diffraction
concepts.description: Wave spreading and the formation of patterns around an aperture or obstacle, beyond a simple ray shadow. In the optical model here, interference between contributions from different parts of an illuminated aperture explains the pattern.

relations.note: The scoped single-slit explanation uses phase-dependent cancellation of wave contributions.
Diffraction is an essential wave correction to ray propagation.

concepts.title: Dirac Delta Function
concepts.description: A distribution that evaluates a test function at a specified point, used to represent idealized point-supported sources and continuous-basis normalization.

relations.note: The introductory distribution pairing is written using the test-function integral and a limiting point source.
The Dirac distribution is the point source defining a Green kernel.
Canonical equal-time field commutators contain spatial Dirac distributions.
A point charge is a delta-supported source of the electrostatic Poisson equation.

concepts.title: Dirac Equation
concepts.description: A first-order Lorentz-covariant equation for a spinor describing spin-one-half matter, interpreted as a field equation in quantum field theory.

relations.note: This applies to the Dirac-field example, not every fermionic field.

concepts.title: Divergence
concepts.description: The scalar differential operator obtained by summing the matching coordinate partial derivatives of a vector field.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped divergence formulation.
Needed for the scoped divergence formulation.

concepts.title: Dot Product
concepts.description: A scalar-valued operation on two real Euclidean vectors of the same dimension, calculated by summing the products of corresponding Cartesian components. It measures directional alignment: for nonzero vectors, it equals their lengths multiplied by the cosine of the angle between them. A vector’s dot product with itself is its squared length.

relations.note: Uses real vector components and elementary vector geometry.

concepts.title: Driven Harmonic Oscillator
concepts.description: A linear restoring-force oscillator family with an externally prescribed drive and optional linear damping, including zero drive as a limiting case. Its motion combines homogeneous transients with a forced response; sinusoidal forcing reveals frequency-dependent amplitude and phase.

relations.note: Setting the prescribed drive to zero recovers the free damped oscillator family.
The sinusoidally forced linear model is a standard quantitative example of resonance.

concepts.title: Dynamic Viscosity
concepts.description: The coefficient relating viscous shear stress to shear rate in a Newtonian fluid. It measures resistance to relative deformation and has SI unit pascal-second.

concepts.title: Dyson Series
concepts.description: The time-ordered expansion of quantum evolution generated by an interaction-picture Hamiltonian, organizing perturbative amplitudes by powers of the interaction.

concepts.title: Effective Mass
concepts.description: A band-curvature parameter describing how a wave packet responds to forces within a crystalline energy band.

relations.note: The band-curvature tensor is calculated from an energy dispersion.
The inverse effective-mass tensor uses second wavevector derivatives.
Effective masses describe carrier acceleration in crystalline bands.

concepts.title: Effective Potential
concepts.description: A reduced potential that incorporates eliminated degrees of freedom or fixed conserved quantities. In a conservative central-force problem, fixing angular momentum adds a centrifugal term to the physical potential, leaving a one-dimensional radial energy equation.

relations.note: At fixed angular momentum it encodes radial turning points and circular-orbit stability.

concepts.title: Ehrenfest Theorem
concepts.description: A relation between the time derivatives of quantum expectation values and Hamiltonian dynamics, yielding mean position and mean force equations.

concepts.title: Eigenvalue
concepts.description: A scalar lambda for a linear operator A such that A v equals lambda v for some nonzero vector v in the operator's domain, called an eigenvector.

relations.note: Discrete measurement values are eigenvalues; continuous spectrum need not have normalizable eigenvectors.

concepts.title: Einstein Field Equations
concepts.description: Equations relating the Einstein tensor and a cosmological term to matter's stress-energy tensor, thereby determining spacetime geometry subject to initial and boundary data.

concepts.title: Einstein Tensor
concepts.description: The symmetric tensor G_ab = R_ab - (1/2) R g_ab, constructed from Ricci curvature and its metric trace; its Levi-Civita covariant divergence vanishes.

concepts.title: Electric Charge
concepts.description: A signed, additive property of matter that determines its electromagnetic interaction.

concepts.title: Electric Current
concepts.description: The signed rate at which electric charge crosses an oriented surface.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped electric current formulation.
Needed for the scoped electric current formulation.

concepts.title: Electric Field
concepts.description: The spatial vector field giving electric force per unit stationary test charge in a chosen frame.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped electric field formulation.
Needed for the scoped electric field formulation.
Needed for the scoped electric field formulation.

concepts.title: Electric Potential
concepts.description: An electrostatic scalar field whose negative gradient gives the electric field and whose difference gives potential-energy change per charge.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped electric potential formulation.
Needed for the scoped electric potential formulation.
Needed for the scoped electric potential formulation.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic Field
concepts.description: The classical field whose electric and magnetic components combine relativistically into an antisymmetric rank-two field-strength tensor, equivalently a spacetime two-form.

relations.note: The relativistic field strength is a differential two-form.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic Wave Equation
concepts.description: The homogeneous wave equations obeyed by electric and magnetic fields in a source-free vacuum.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped electromagnetic wave equation formulation.
Needed for the scoped electromagnetic wave equation formulation.
In source-free vacuum, differentiating the Maxwell system gives the homogeneous wave equations; its original constraints remain necessary.

concepts.title: Electron Configuration
concepts.description: A specification of electron occupations of orbitals or subshells in an atom or molecule. Atomic configurations are commonly written as shell and subshell labels with superscripts giving their electron counts.

relations.note: An atomic configuration specifies occupation of atomic orbitals and their subshell groupings.

concepts.title: Electronic Band Structure
concepts.description: The allowed electron-energy bands and intervening gaps of a solid, described in a periodic crystal by energies indexed by a band label and Bloch wavevector.

relations.note: The periodic-crystal description uses Bloch eigenstates to label the energy bands.
Band structure helps explain electrical conduction and optical properties of solids.

concepts.title: Enthalpy
concepts.description: A thermodynamic potential defined by adding pressure times volume to internal energy. Equality between an enthalpy change and exchanged heat requires additional process conditions.

concepts.title: Equipartition Theorem
concepts.description: A classical equilibrium result assigning an average energy kBT/2 to each independent additive quadratic term in the energy, under the theorem's phase-space assumptions.

relations.note: Equilibrium temperature sets the energy scale kBT.
Canonical averaging of an independent quadratic energy term yields kBT/2.
Counting active quadratic terms predicts classical ideal-gas heat capacities.

concepts.title: Equivalence Principle
concepts.description: In its Einstein form, local nongravitational experiments in a freely falling laboratory obey special relativity; this does not eliminate tidal curvature over a finite region.

concepts.title: Euclidean Vector
concepts.description: An elementary geometric vector represented by a directed displacement in Euclidean space. It has a magnitude and, unless zero, a direction; translating its arrow without changing these leaves the vector unchanged. In n dimensions, Cartesian components form a real n-tuple, with addition and scalar multiplication performed component by component.

concepts.title: Euler-Lagrange Equation
concepts.description: The equation partial L / partial q_i - d/dt(partial L / partial qdot_i) = 0 characterizing sufficiently smooth stationary paths of a first-order action under fixed-endpoint variations.
aliases: Lagrange's equations of the second kind

relations.note: The mechanical equation characterizes stationary paths of the chosen first-order action.
The equation differentiates independent configuration and velocity arguments before evaluating them along a path.
The equation is obtained by setting the first variation to zero.
Arbitrariness of interior variations yields the pointwise equation.
Mechanical equations of motion follow from the chosen Lagrangian.

concepts.title: Event Horizon
concepts.description: For an asymptotically flat black hole, the boundary of the region unable to send future-directed causal signals to future null infinity; it is a global causal boundary.

relations.note: The Schwarzschild black-hole horizon is regular in suitable coordinates and is not a curvature singularity.

concepts.title: Exact Form
concepts.description: A differential form omega of positive degree for which omega = d eta for a globally defined form eta of one lower degree. Every exact form is closed.

concepts.title: Expected Value
concepts.description: The probability-weighted average of a random variable, defined by integration with respect to its probability measure. A finite expectation exists when the absolute value is integrable; some distributions have no finite mean.

relations.note: Expectation summarizes a random variable.
Its probability law supplies the weights used in the average.
Ensemble expectations calculate mean physical observables such as energy.

concepts.title: Exterior Derivative
concepts.description: The natural differential operator d that raises the degree of a differential form by one, extends differentiation of functions, obeys the graded product rule, and satisfies d squared equals zero.

relations.note: The wedge product enters the defining graded product rule.
Local expressions differentiate the coefficient functions of a differential form.
Coordinate expressions use partial derivatives of form coefficients.

concepts.title: Fermi–Dirac Statistics
concepts.description: Quantum statistics for identical fermions, with at most one particle in each complete single-particle state; for noninteracting particles it yields the Fermi–Dirac occupation distribution.

relations.note: Fermionic state counting permits occupation zero or one per complete one-particle state.
The occupation depends on energy relative to the chemical potential.
Independent fermionic occupation sums in the grand canonical ensemble yield this distribution.

concepts.title: Fermi Energy
concepts.description: The zero-temperature energy difference between the highest and lowest occupied single-particle levels of noninteracting fermions, setting a characteristic degeneracy energy scale.

relations.note: Exclusion forces ground-state fermions to fill successively higher available single-particle states.
Fermi energy supplies the degeneracy scale of the ideal fermion gas.

concepts.title: Fermi Gas
concepts.description: An ideal many-particle model of noninteracting identical fermions whose equilibrium populations obey Fermi–Dirac statistics.

relations.note: The ideal gas's single-particle populations obey Fermi–Dirac statistics.
The free-electron gas is an introductory approximation for electronic properties of metals.

concepts.title: Fermi's Golden Rule
concepts.description: A weak-coupling approximation for the transition rate from an initial quantum energy eigenstate into an accessible continuum of final states.

relations.note: The continuum rate follows from first-order time-dependent transition amplitudes.
Weak-potential scattering rates can be converted into cross sections.

concepts.title: Fermi Surface
concepts.description: The zero-temperature occupied-to-unoccupied boundary in momentum or crystal-wavevector space, located at the chemical potential when a band or quasiparticle description is applicable.

relations.note: At zero temperature the occupied-state boundary is determined by the chemical potential, measured in the same energy convention as the band energies.
The zero-temperature occupancy limit explains the boundary.
Partially filled bands determine metallic Fermi surfaces.

concepts.title: Fermion
concepts.description: A particle with half-integer spin whose identical-particle quantum states are antisymmetric under exchange, obeying the Pauli exclusion principle in ordinary three-dimensional physics.

relations.note: Half-integer intrinsic spin characterizes fermions in the ordinary spin-statistics setting.
Fermi–Dirac state counting applies to identical fermions.

concepts.title: Fermionic Field
concepts.description: A quantum field whose excitations obey fermionic statistics, with the free Dirac field providing the introductory spin-one-half example.

concepts.title: Feynman Diagram
concepts.description: A graphical representation of a term in a perturbative expansion of quantum-field correlation functions or amplitudes, with lines and vertices encoding mathematical factors rather than literal particle trajectories.

concepts.title: Field Action
concepts.description: A functional of complete field configurations obtained by integrating a Lagrangian density over a spacetime region, with admissible variations and boundary data specified.

concepts.title: Field Euler–Lagrange Equation
concepts.description: For a first-order local field action, the equation partial L / partial phi_a minus partial_mu(partial L / partial(partial_mu phi_a)) = 0 obtained from stationarity under admissible variations with vanishing boundary terms.

concepts.title: Finite Potential Well
concepts.description: A quantum confinement model with a finite-depth low-potential region; bound-state wavefunctions extend beyond its edges and only finitely many bound levels occur in the one-dimensional square well.

relations.note: Bound energies are selected by continuity and normalizability of wavefunctions.
Piecewise stationary solutions and matching determine the bound-state conditions.

concepts.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
concepts.description: Energy conservation for thermodynamic processes; for a closed system with unchanged bulk kinetic and potential energies, ΔU = Q − W, with heat Q entering and work W done by the system.
aliases: First law of thermodynamics energy balance

relations.note: The energy balance distinguishes stored energy from transfer.
The law constrains energy exchange.

concepts.title: First Variation
concepts.description: The first-order change of a differentiable functional under an admissible perturbation, computed as d J[y + epsilon eta] / d epsilon at epsilon = 0.

relations.note: Variations differentiate functionals with respect to perturbations.
The first variation differentiates the perturbed functional with respect to its scalar perturbation parameter.
Stationarity requires the first variation to vanish for all admissible perturbations.

concepts.title: FLRW Spacetime
concepts.description: A family of spacetime geometries with homogeneous and isotropic spatial slices and a time-dependent cosmic scale factor.

relations.note: The construction specifies the spacetime interval through a metric.
Homogeneous and isotropic spatial slices are the defining symmetry assumptions.
Inserting this ansatz and compatible matter into Einstein’s equations yields Friedmann evolution.
The FLRW geometry supplies homogeneous cosmological background models.

concepts.title: Fluid Continuity Equation
concepts.description: The local conservation equation for fluid mass, relating the rate of density change to the divergence of the mass flux.

concepts.title: Fluid Mechanics
concepts.description: The study of liquids and gases at rest and in motion, treating their bulk properties and forces within a continuum description.

concepts.title: Fock Space
concepts.description: The Hilbert direct sum of all n-particle sectors including the vacuum sector, constructed from symmetric tensor powers of a one-particle space for bosons or antisymmetric powers for fermions.

relations.note: Fock representations describe free particles and perturbative asymptotic states, not every interacting representation without qualification.

concepts.title: Force
concepts.description: A vector quantity representing a mechanical interaction that contributes to the change of a body's momentum. In Newtonian particle mechanics, the net force is the vector sum of the forces acting on that particle.

relations.note: Forces in ordinary Euclidean mechanics combine by geometric vector addition.
A conservative force is the restricted class with path-independent work; general forces need not have this property.

concepts.title: Four-Momentum
concepts.description: The spacetime momentum vector combining energy and spatial momentum; p^a = m u^a for massive particles, while massless particles have nonzero null four-momentum.

concepts.title: Four-Vector
concepts.description: A spacetime tangent vector whose four components transform by Lorentz transformations in inertial coordinates; arbitrary collections of four numbers need not form one.

concepts.title: Four-Velocity
concepts.description: The tangent u^a = dx^a/dτ to a timelike worldline parameterized by proper time, with metric norm -c² in mostly-plus signature.

relations.note: For a massive point particle with rest mass m, p^a = m u^a.

concepts.title: Fourier Transform
concepts.description: A linear transform representing a suitable function by continuous frequency or wave-number components. Its integral definition, inversion and extensions depend on the chosen normalization and function space.

relations.note: The introductory integral representation uses calculus; generalized transforms require additional function-space and convergence machinery.
For suitable functions, Fourier transformation turns constant-coefficient differential operators into frequency-space multipliers.
Fourier transformation relates spacetime and momentum-space propagators, with the appropriate distributional prescription.
Relates position and wave-number or momentum representations, with the appropriate normalization and momentum p = hbar k.

concepts.title: Friedmann Equations
concepts.description: The Einstein-equation constraints and evolution equations for homogeneous, isotropic expansion sourced by cosmological matter and pressure.

relations.note: They follow from Einstein’s equations after imposing FLRW symmetry and compatible stress-energy.
The expansion variable and spatial curvature come from the FLRW geometry.
Matter energy density and isotropic pressure provide the sources.

concepts.title: Functional
concepts.description: A scalar-valued map whose arguments are functions or paths; in variational problems it assigns a number to each admissible candidate.

relations.note: Variational functionals commonly depend on functions and their derivatives.
An action is a particular functional used to specify dynamics.
A field action is a scalar-valued functional of field configurations.

concepts.title: Fundamental Lemma of Calculus of Variations
concepts.description: If a continuous function on an open interval has zero integral against every smooth compactly supported test function, then it vanishes throughout that interval.
aliases: Fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations

relations.note: The statement relates integrals and arbitrary smooth test functions.
The lemma converts the integrated stationarity condition into a differential equation.

concepts.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.description: For continuous f on a closed interval, the accumulated integral of f has derivative f in the interior, and any antiderivative F evaluates the interval integral as F(b) minus F(a).

concepts.title: Gauge Symmetry
concepts.description: A redundancy of field variables under transformations that identify physically equivalent configurations; which transformations count as gauge depends on the constraints and boundary conditions.

relations.note: Different admissible potential descriptions can encode the same electromagnetic field strength.
Gauge descriptions must preserve the physical state space and observables.

concepts.title: General Relativity
concepts.description: The relativistic theory of gravitation in which matter and energy are related to the geometry of curved spacetime through Einstein's field equations.

relations.note: Special relativity is recovered in the flat-spacetime, nongravitating limit and locally in freely falling frames.

concepts.title: Generalized Coordinate
concepts.description: One of a set of independent local parameters specifying a mechanical configuration; these need not be Cartesian positions.

relations.note: The coordinates label points of configuration space.
A cyclic coordinate is a generalized coordinate absent from the chosen Lagrangian.

concepts.title: Generalized Momentum
concepts.description: The momentum conjugate to q_i, defined by p_i = partial L / partial qdot_i; it need not equal mass times Cartesian velocity.

relations.note: Conjugate momentum differentiates the Lagrangian with respect to velocity.
The velocity derivative holds the other independent Lagrangian arguments fixed.
Conjugate momenta replace velocities in a regular Hamiltonian formulation.
Conjugate momenta provide the momentum coordinates in the canonical Hamiltonian representation of phase space.

concepts.title: Geodesic
concepts.description: A curve that parallel-transports its own tangent; for a metric-compatible Levi-Civita connection it describes locally straight motion and, with suitable qualification, extremal interval or length.

relations.note: Geodesics describe idealized free-fall and light propagation in Schwarzschild spacetime.
Geodesics model idealized freely falling test particles and light rays in general relativity.

concepts.title: Geodesic Deviation
concepts.description: The curvature-controlled relative acceleration of nearby geodesics, expressed by the Jacobi equation; in spacetime it describes tidal gravitational effects.

concepts.title: Geodesic Equation
concepts.description: The affine-parameter equation ∇_v v = 0 for a curve's tangent v; coordinate connection terms compensate for a changing local basis.

concepts.title: Geometric Phase
concepts.description: A phase contribution determined by the geometry of a quantum-state path, distinct from the phase accumulated from energy and elapsed time.

concepts.title: Geometrical Optics
concepts.description: An approximation that follows light rays to predict reflection, refraction and image formation when diffraction can be neglected at the scale of interest. Rays are straight in a homogeneous medium and can bend when the refractive index varies.

concepts.title: Gibbs Free Energy
concepts.description: The thermodynamic potential G=U+pV−TS, suited to comparing equilibrium states at controlled temperature and pressure.

relations.note: Gibbs free energy subtracts TS from enthalpy.
Its thermal Legendre transform uses entropy.
At fixed temperature and pressure, competing phases are compared through their Gibbs potentials.

concepts.title: Gradient
concepts.description: For a differentiable scalar function on Euclidean space, the vector of coordinate partial derivatives that represents its differential using the Euclidean inner product.

relations.note: On a Riemannian manifold the metric identifies the differential with a gradient vector field.

concepts.title: Grand Canonical Ensemble
concepts.description: An equilibrium statistical ensemble for a system exchanging energy and particles with reservoirs, at fixed temperature, chemical potentials, and mechanical parameters such as volume.

concepts.title: Gravitational Time Dilation
concepts.description: Differences between clock proper-time rates associated with gravitational geometry; comparing stationary clocks requires a specified stationary setting and a common time normalization.

relations.note: For static observers outside r = 2GM/c², dτ = sqrt(1 - 2GM/(rc²)) dt when t is normalized at infinity.

concepts.title: Green's Function
concepts.description: A kernel solving a linear differential operator's point-source equation with specified boundary or initial conditions, allowing compatible distributed sources to be treated by superposition.

relations.note: Superposition and the response-kernel construction require a linear operator.
The kernel's defining source is a Dirac distribution.
Electrostatic Green kernels reconstruct Poisson solutions for charge distributions and specified boundary data.
Free-field Feynman propagators are Green kernels up to a convention-dependent constant and pole prescription.

concepts.title: Group
concepts.description: A set equipped with an associative binary operation, an identity element, and an inverse for every element.

relations.note: Groups encode composable invertible transformations.
Lie groups add compatible smooth structure.

concepts.title: Group Homomorphism
concepts.description: A map between groups that preserves multiplication, f(ab) = f(a)f(b), and therefore preserves identity elements and inverses.

relations.note: The map respects group operations.
A representation is a homomorphism into invertible linear maps.

concepts.title: Group Representation
concepts.description: A homomorphism from a group to the invertible linear transformations of a vector space, representing group multiplication by composition of linear maps.

relations.note: Multiplication must be preserved.
The representation acts by invertible linear maps.
Irreducibility adds an invariant-subspace restriction.
Representations describe rotational symmetry and angular-momentum states.

concepts.title: Group Theory
concepts.description: The mathematical study of groups, their structure, and their representations, providing a language for discrete and continuous symmetries.

relations.note: Groups are the basic objects.
Symmetry groups organize quantum states and transformations.

concepts.title: Hamilton–Jacobi Equation
concepts.description: A first-order partial differential equation for Hamilton's principal function in classical Hamiltonian mechanics. Its coordinate derivatives give canonical momenta, while its time derivative is minus the Hamiltonian evaluated at those momenta.

relations.note: Endpoint variation of the action evaluated on stationary classical trajectories yields the equation.
Describes the leading classical-action equation in suitable semiclassical approximations, not exact quantum evolution.

concepts.title: Hamiltonian
concepts.description: A classical phase-space function H(q, p, t) generating Hamilton's equations; for a regular Lagrangian it can be constructed locally by Legendre transformation in the velocity variables.

relations.note: The classical Hamiltonian is a function of a system's phase-space state and possibly time.
The standard passage from a regular Lagrangian uses a Legendre transform.
Canonical momenta are phase-space variables.
Classical equilibrium ensembles use phase-space energies.

concepts.title: Hamiltonian Mechanics
concepts.description: A formulation of classical dynamics on phase space in which a Hamiltonian function generates the evolution of canonical coordinates and momenta through Hamilton's equations.

relations.note: Finite-dimensional Hamiltonian evolution is a system of first-order ordinary differential equations.

concepts.title: Heat
concepts.description: Energy transferred across a system boundary because of a temperature difference; it is a process quantity rather than energy stored in a state.

relations.note: A temperature difference identifies this mode of energy transfer.
Signed heat input enters the closed-system energy balance.

concepts.title: Heat Capacity
concepts.description: A system's thermal response under specified constraints, relating heat input to temperature change; constant-volume and constant-pressure heat capacities are distinct.

relations.note: Heat capacity connects constrained heat input with thermal response.
The response is measured per change in temperature.

concepts.title: Heat Engine
concepts.description: A device that produces net work by taking in heat and rejecting part of it, typically through a cycle of its working substance.

relations.note: Heat received and rejected are inputs to the engine's energy accounting.
Zero stored-energy change over a cycle relates net heat to net work.
The second law limits conversion efficiency between thermal reservoirs.

concepts.title: Heisenberg Equation of Motion
concepts.description: An operator evolution law expressing Hamiltonian-generated change as a commutator, with an extra term for explicit time dependence.

concepts.title: Helmholtz Free Energy
concepts.description: The thermodynamic potential obtained by subtracting temperature times entropy from internal energy. In the usual closed-system setting it is minimized at equilibrium under fixed temperature, volume, and particle number.

concepts.title: Hilbert Space
concepts.description: An inner product space in which every Cauchy sequence for the induced norm converges to an element of the space.

relations.note: Complex Hilbert spaces provide the standard state-space framework.
A Fock space is a Hilbert space with a specified particle-sector construction.

concepts.title: Holonomic Constraint
concepts.description: A mechanical constraint expressible as an equation among configuration variables and possibly time, without an independent dependence on velocities.

relations.note: The constraint restricts the permitted configurations.
Regular holonomic constraints can be eliminated using suitable generalized coordinates.
The fixed pivot-to-bob distance is a holonomic constraint in a constrained-mechanics description of the ideal pendulum.

concepts.title: Hubble Parameter
concepts.description: The instantaneous fractional expansion rate of the cosmic scale factor, whose present value is called the Hubble constant.

relations.note: The parameter is the logarithmic time derivative of the scale factor.
It measures an instantaneous rate of fractional change.
Friedmann evolution relates H to matter and spatial curvature.

concepts.title: Huygens's Principle
concepts.description: A construction for advancing a wavefront: each point on the current front launches secondary wavelets, and their forward envelope gives the next front. It helps visualize reflection, refraction and spreading at an aperture.

relations.note: Advancing wavefronts at a reflecting boundary recovers equal ray angles.
Wavefront geometry with two propagation speeds yields the refraction law.
Secondary contributions across an aperture provide the introductory wave picture.

concepts.title: Hydrogen-like Atom
concepts.description: An atom or ion consisting of a nucleus and one electron. Its simplest bound-state model is a two-body Coulomb problem with an analytic nonrelativistic spectrum.

relations.note: The introductory spectrum follows from the stationary Coulomb Schrödinger problem.
Electrostatic attraction sets the central binding potential.
The relative-coordinate mass accounts for nuclear as well as electronic motion.

concepts.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium
concepts.description: Mechanical balance in a fluid at rest, where pressure gradients balance body forces such as gravity.

concepts.title: Ideal Gas
concepts.description: A gas model that neglects molecular excluded volume and interaction energy, providing an approximation to sufficiently dilute classical gases.

relations.note: Negligible molecular volume and non-collision interactions define the basic kinetic gas model.

concepts.title: Ideal Gas Law
concepts.description: The equilibrium equation of state pV = NkBT = nRT relating an ideal gas's pressure, volume, temperature, and amount.

relations.note: The equation describes the ideal-gas model and approximates sufficiently dilute real gases.
The pressure in the equation is absolute pressure.
The temperature in the equation is absolute temperature.

concepts.title: Index Raising and Lowering
concepts.description: The metric-induced identification between tangent and cotangent vectors, extended to tensor slots; lowering uses the metric and raising uses its inverse.

concepts.title: Inertial Reference Frame
concepts.description: A nonaccelerating coordinate frame in which free particles move uniformly along straight lines; global inertial frames are available in Minkowski spacetime.

relations.note: The introductory Newtonian criterion identifies unaccelerated free-particle motion.
The free-particle criterion refers to motion without a net force.

concepts.title: Infinitesimal Strain
concepts.description: The symmetric part of the displacement gradient, used as a linear approximation to local deformation when displacement gradients are small.

concepts.title: Initial Value Problem
concepts.description: A differential equation or system supplied with values of its unknown state at one independent-variable value. These initial data select a trajectory when suitable existence and uniqueness conditions hold; the data alone do not guarantee a well-posed problem.

relations.note: The introductory route here treats ordinary differential equations; initial-data problems for PDEs require further structure.
Mechanical prediction requires suitable initial positions and velocities or equivalent state data.

concepts.title: Inner Product Space
concepts.description: A real or complex vector space with a positive-definite symmetric bilinear or Hermitian sesquilinear form, which determines lengths and orthogonality.

relations.note: A Hilbert space is complete in the norm induced by its inner product.

concepts.title: Integration of Differential Forms
concepts.description: Coordinate-independent integration of compactly supported smooth k-forms over oriented k-dimensional smooth manifolds, defined through pullbacks in oriented charts and a partition of unity.

relations.note: Integrals over cycles can detect nonzero cohomology classes.

concepts.title: Interaction Picture
concepts.description: A representation that splits the Hamiltonian so operators carry a chosen reference evolution and states carry the remaining interaction evolution.

concepts.title: Interference
concepts.description: The reinforcement or cancellation produced when overlapping waves add with their relative phase taken into account. For light, fields superpose and the resulting intensity can show bright and dark fringes when the phase relationship remains stable.

relations.note: Coherent wave superposition accounts for optical fringe patterns.

concepts.title: Interior Product
concepts.description: The operation i_X that inserts a smooth vector field X into the first argument of a differential k-form, producing a (k-1)-form for positive k and acting as zero on functions.

relations.note: On differential forms, Cartan's formula is L_X = d i_X + i_X d.

concepts.title: Internal Energy
concepts.description: A thermodynamic state function accounting for energy stored within a system, excluding kinetic and external potential energy associated with the system as a whole.

relations.note: Its change enters the energy balance.
Internal energy is an equilibrium state variable.

concepts.title: Inverse Metric
concepts.description: The contravariant rank-two tensor whose coordinate matrix is inverse to the metric matrix, satisfying g^{ac} g_cb = δ^a_b.

concepts.title: Irreducible Representation
concepts.description: A nonzero linear group representation with no invariant subspaces except the zero subspace and the whole representation space.

relations.note: Irreducibility is a property of a representation.
Rotational multiplets are organized by irreducible representations.

concepts.title: Ising Model
concepts.description: A lattice model of interacting binary variables, used to study magnetic ordering, phase transitions, and equivalent lattice-gas behavior.

relations.note: Equilibrium Ising probabilities and thermodynamics are constructed from its partition function.
The model exhibits phase transitions for suitable dimension, coupling, and field.
Ising variables provide simplified descriptions of magnetic ordering in solids.

concepts.title: Isobaric Process
concepts.description: A thermodynamic process in which the system pressure remains constant while other state variables can change.

relations.note: The pressure of the system is the constrained variable.
Constant-pressure heating defines the C_p thermal response.

concepts.title: Isochoric Process
concepts.description: A thermodynamic process at constant system volume; it has no pressure-volume boundary work, although other forms of work may still occur.

relations.note: Fixed-volume heating isolates the C_V response when no other work occurs.

concepts.title: Isothermal Process
concepts.description: A thermodynamic process during which the system temperature stays constant; heat may be exchanged and other state variables may change.

relations.note: The defining constraint fixes temperature during the process.
Two reversible isothermal stages exchange heat at the reservoir temperatures.

concepts.title: Isotropic Hooke Law
concepts.description: The linear elastic constitutive relation between Cauchy stress and infinitesimal strain in an isotropic material, determined by two independent elastic moduli.

concepts.title: Kepler Orbit
concepts.description: A trajectory in an attractive inverse-square central force. Nonradial Newtonian two-body relative trajectories are conic sections: circles or ellipses for bound motion, a parabola at zero relative energy, and hyperbolas for positive relative energy.

relations.note: The gravitational two-body case follows from the attractive inverse-square law and the relative equation of motion.

concepts.title: Kinematics
concepts.description: The description of motion through positions, velocities, accelerations, and their time dependence, without specifying the forces responsible for that motion.

relations.note: Kinematic quantities describe the trajectories that Newtonian dynamics predicts.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy
concepts.description: The energy associated with motion in a specified reference frame. For a nonrelativistic particle it is one half the mass times the squared speed; a system's particle kinetic energies add.

relations.note: For a standard mechanical system with a velocity-independent potential, the Lagrangian is kinetic energy minus potential energy.
For the standard Cartesian particle model, the Hamiltonian contains kinetic energy expressed in canonical momenta.

concepts.title: Kinetic Theory of Gases
concepts.description: The microscopic study of gas behavior through molecular motion and collisions, connecting statistical averages to pressure, temperature, and transport.

relations.note: Classical molecular trajectories and collisions obey Newtonian mechanics.
Molecular momentum transport gives kinetic estimates of dilute-gas viscosity.

concepts.title: Klein–Gordon Equation
concepts.description: A Lorentz-covariant second-order wave equation for a free massive scalar field; its quantum-field interpretation describes spin-zero excitations.

relations.note: The introductory derivation starts with a classical scalar field.

concepts.title: Kruskal–Szekeres Coordinates
concepts.description: Coordinates regular across the Schwarzschild horizons that describe its maximal analytic extension, exposing black-hole, white-hole and two exterior regions without removing the r = 0 singularity.

concepts.title: Lagrange Multiplier
concepts.description: An auxiliary coefficient enforcing an equality constraint in stationarity equations; under suitable regularity conditions it expresses the objective derivative as a combination of constraint derivatives.

relations.note: Multiplier equations use derivatives and regularity of constraints.
Time-dependent multipliers can enforce mechanical position constraints.
Multipliers incorporate regular constraints into variational equations.
Equilibrium probabilities can be obtained by constrained entropy maximization.

concepts.title: Lagrangian
concepts.description: A function L(q, qdot, t) of configuration, velocity and time whose time integral defines the mechanical action; for standard conservative particle systems it is kinetic minus potential energy.

relations.note: Mechanical Lagrangians are expressed in generalized coordinates and velocities.
Integrating the Lagrangian along a trajectory constructs the mechanical action.

concepts.title: Lagrangian Density
concepts.description: A local spacetime density built from fields and, in first-order models, their first derivatives, whose spacetime integral defines the field action.

concepts.title: Lagrangian Energy
concepts.description: The function E_L = sum_i qdot_i p_i - L; along Euler-Lagrange trajectories it is conserved when the Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence.

relations.note: The energy function pairs each velocity with its conjugate momentum.
Its evolution obeys dE_L/dt = -partial L/partial t on solutions.

concepts.title: Lagrangian Mechanics
concepts.description: A formulation of classical mechanics in which equations of motion follow from a Lagrangian and a stationary-action variational principle rather than directly from force balance.

relations.note: The formulation begins with a Lagrangian for the system.
Lagrangian mechanics is a formulation of classical mechanical dynamics, not a distinct special-case theory.

concepts.title: Landau Theory
concepts.description: A phenomenological approach that models phase behavior using a symmetry-compatible expansion of a thermodynamic potential in an order parameter.

relations.note: The theory models phase transitions through the behavior of a chosen order parameter.
At fixed volume and temperature the stable phase minimizes the Helmholtz potential.
The phenomenological potential is expanded in powers of a small order parameter.

concepts.title: Law of Reflection
concepts.description: For specular reflection, the reflected ray makes the same angle with the surface normal as the incident ray. The incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane.

relations.note: It determines reflected ray directions in ray tracing.

concepts.title: Legendre Transform
concepts.description: A change from a variable x to its conjugate p = grad f(x), producing g(p) = p dot x - f(x) where the gradient map can be inverted; this record concerns the smooth local transform.

relations.note: The smooth local transform uses derivatives in the transformed variables while holding other arguments fixed.
A regular velocity-to-momentum transformation converts a Lagrangian into a Hamiltonian.

concepts.title: Length Contraction
concepts.description: An object's length parallel to uniform relative motion, measured using simultaneous endpoint positions in the observer's inertial frame, is its rest length divided by γ.

concepts.title: Levi-Civita Connection
concepts.description: The unique affine connection associated with a metric that is torsion-free and compatible with that metric.

relations.note: It is uniquely determined by the metric through the Koszul formula.

concepts.title: Lie Algebra
concepts.description: A vector space over the real or complex numbers with a bilinear antisymmetric bracket satisfying the Jacobi identity; a Lie group's tangent space at the identity carries such a bracket.

relations.note: The bracket is a bilinear operation on a vector space.
The associated Lie algebra describes infinitesimal group structure.
Commutators encode continuous-symmetry generators.

concepts.title: Lie Derivative
concepts.description: The rate of change of a tensor field measured after transporting it back along the local flow generated by a smooth vector field, which on differential forms obeys Cartan's formula L_X = d i_X + i_X d.

concepts.title: Lie Group
concepts.description: A finite-dimensional smooth manifold with a group structure whose multiplication and inversion maps are smooth.

relations.note: A Lie group has a group operation.
Group operations are compatible with a smooth manifold.
Continuous symmetry groups organize quantum transformations.

concepts.title: Light Cone
concepts.description: In Minkowski spacetime, the null-separated events around an event form its past and future light cones; in curved spacetime the metric defines tangent-space null cones.

concepts.title: Limit of a Function
concepts.description: A value approached by a function as its input approaches a specified accumulation point, independently of the function's value at that point.

relations.note: Limits define local change and accumulation.

concepts.title: Line Element
concepts.description: The coordinate expression ds² = g_ab dx^a dx^b for a metric's infinitesimal quadratic interval; it need not be positive in indefinite signature.

concepts.title: Linear Algebra
concepts.description: The study of vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, eigenvalues, and inner products that supplies core mathematical language for classical and quantum physics.

relations.note: Vector and operator techniques support physical models.

concepts.title: Linear Map
concepts.description: A map between vector spaces over the same field that preserves addition and scalar multiplication.

relations.note: A linear operator acts in one ambient vector space, possibly on a specified linear domain.

concepts.title: Linear Momentum
concepts.description: The translational momentum of a particle or system. For a Newtonian particle it is mass times velocity; the total momentum of a particle system is the vector sum of its constituent momenta.

relations.note: For a standard Cartesian particle Lagrangian without a velocity-dependent potential, the canonical momentum equals the Newtonian linear momentum.

concepts.title: Linear Operator
concepts.description: A linear map from a vector space into itself, or from a specified linear subspace of its domain into that same ambient space when treating partially defined operators.
aliases: Linear operator on a vector space

relations.note: Self-adjointness imposes an adjoint and domain condition in a Hilbert space.

concepts.title: Lorentz Boost
concepts.description: A Lorentz transformation between inertial frames in relative uniform motion with no added spatial rotation; it mixes time with the direction of motion.

concepts.title: Lorentz Force
concepts.description: The total classical force on a point charge from electric and magnetic fields in a specified inertial frame.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped lorentz force formulation.
Needed for the scoped lorentz force formulation.
Needed for the scoped lorentz force formulation.
Needed for the scoped lorentz force formulation.

concepts.title: Lorentz Group
concepts.description: The Lie group O(1,3) of real linear transformations preserving the Minkowski bilinear form, including rotations, boosts, and disconnected parity or time-reversal components.

relations.note: Lorentz transformations form a six-dimensional matrix Lie group.
The defining matrix condition preserves the Minkowski metric.
Lorentz symmetry relates inertial-coordinate descriptions in special relativity.
Relativistic electromagnetic fields transform under Lorentz representations.

concepts.title: Lorentz Transformation
concepts.description: A linear transformation preserving the Minkowski metric and spacetime interval; Lorentz transformations include spatial rotations and boosts, but not translations.

relations.note: Pure boosts form a class of Lorentz transformations, not a subgroup by themselves.

concepts.title: Lorentzian Manifold
concepts.description: A pseudo-Riemannian manifold whose metric has one timelike and the remaining spacelike directions, providing the geometric model of relativistic spacetime.

concepts.title: Macrostate
concepts.description: A specification of macroscopic observables or constraints that generally leaves many compatible microscopic states unresolved.

relations.note: Coarse macroscopic information groups compatible microstates.
Compatible-state multiplicity defines Boltzmann entropy.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field
concepts.description: The axial field B that determines the magnetic force on moving electric charges.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped magnetic field formulation.
Needed for the scoped magnetic field formulation.
Needed for the scoped magnetic field formulation.
Needed for the scoped magnetic field formulation.

concepts.title: Magnetic Quantum Number
concepts.description: A dimensionless label m for the projection of a quantum angular momentum along a chosen axis. Orbital, spin and total-angular-momentum projections have their own magnetic quantum numbers.

relations.note: The number labels an angular momentum projection eigenvalue.
Magnetic sublevels acquire projection-dependent energy shifts.

concepts.title: Manifold
concepts.description: A Hausdorff, second-countable topological space locally modeled on Euclidean space of a fixed dimension. This record uses the convention of manifolds without boundary.

relations.note: A smooth manifold adds a compatible smooth atlas to an underlying topological manifold.

concepts.title: Manifold Orientation
concepts.description: A globally compatible, continuously varying choice of orientation for the tangent space at every point of a smooth manifold, available precisely when the manifold is orientable.

relations.note: The chosen orientation determines the sign of an integral of a top-degree form.

concepts.title: Mass Density
concepts.description: Mass per unit volume. In a continuum it may vary with position and time; total mass divided by total volume gives the volume-average density.

concepts.title: Mathematical Methods
concepts.description: Mathematical techniques used to formulate, analyze, and approximate physical models, including calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, and variational methods.

relations.note: Calculus supplies differential and integral techniques.
Linear algebra supplies vector and operator techniques.
Variational methods formulate equations of motion.
Linear and differential methods analyze quantum models.

concepts.title: Matrix
concepts.description: A rectangular array of scalars with specified row and column dimensions, used to represent linear maps once bases have been chosen in finite-dimensional spaces.

relations.note: Matrix multiplication expresses the coordinate action and composition of finite-dimensional linear maps.
Matrices represent the inertia tensor in the general three-dimensional extension; the scalar moment about a fixed axis does not require this representation.

concepts.title: Maxwell–Boltzmann Speed Distribution
concepts.description: The equilibrium probability density for molecular speed in a classical gas, obtained by summing the velocity distribution over directions in three dimensions.

relations.note: Probabilities for speed intervals are integrals of a normalized density.
The translational Boltzmann weight uses the nonrelativistic energy mv²/2.
Integrating the kinetic-energy Boltzmann weight over velocity directions supplies the 4πv² factor.

concepts.title: Maxwell’s Equations
