concepts.description: Four coupled classical field equations relating electric and magnetic fields to total charge and current densities.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped maxwell’s equations formulation.
Needed for the scoped maxwell’s equations formulation.
Needed for the scoped maxwell’s equations formulation.
Needed for the scoped maxwell’s equations formulation.
Needed for the scoped maxwell’s equations formulation.

concepts.title: Maxwell Relations
concepts.description: Thermodynamic derivative identities obtained from equality of mixed derivatives of smooth thermodynamic potentials.

relations.note: The identities compare second mixed derivatives of state functions.
The displayed identity follows from the differential of the Helmholtz potential.
Maxwell identities connect thermal response functions such as heat capacities to other measurable derivatives.

concepts.title: Mean-Field Theory
concepts.description: An approximation replacing the fluctuating influence of surrounding degrees of freedom with an effective average, often determined self-consistently.

relations.note: The effective field is determined by suitable averages.
A uniform mean-field approximation yields a self-consistency equation for Ising magnetization.

concepts.title: Mean Free Path
concepts.description: In gas kinetic theory, the average distance a molecule travels between successive collisions with other molecules.

relations.note: A distribution of free-flight distances defines their mean.
The molecular flight distance enters kinetic estimates of momentum transport and viscosity.

concepts.title: Metric
concepts.description: A smooth nondegenerate symmetric covariant rank-two tensor that defines lengths, angles, and volume in Riemannian geometry, and invariant intervals and causal structure when it has Lorentzian signature.

relations.note: The Minkowski metric is a particular flat Lorentzian metric.

concepts.title: Metric Compatibility
concepts.description: The property ∇g = 0 of a connection relative to a metric, ensuring that parallel transport preserves metric pairings.

concepts.title: Metric Signature
concepts.description: The basis-independent counts of positive and negative directions of a nondegenerate real symmetric metric; Lorentzian signature has one direction of the opposite sign.

concepts.title: Metric Volume Form
concepts.description: On an oriented pseudo-Riemannian manifold, the metric determines a top-degree form with coordinate factor sqrt(|det g|); without orientation it determines a volume density.

concepts.title: Microcanonical Ensemble
concepts.description: An equilibrium ensemble of an isolated system with fixed conserved quantities, assigning equal statistical weight to accessible states in a specified narrow energy range.

relations.note: This is an ensemble with isolation constraints.
Accessible-state multiplicity yields the microcanonical entropy.

concepts.title: Microstate
concepts.description: A complete microscopic specification of a system in its chosen model, such as particle positions and momenta classically or a pure quantum state.

relations.note: Many microscopic configurations can realize one macrostate.
Ensembles assign probabilities over microscopic states.

concepts.title: Minkowski Metric
concepts.description: The flat Lorentzian metric of Minkowski spacetime, represented in inertial Cartesian coordinates by diag(-1, 1, 1, 1) when x⁰ = ct.

concepts.title: Minkowski Spacetime
concepts.description: The flat four-dimensional spacetime of special relativity, equipped with the Lorentzian Minkowski metric and no gravitational curvature.

concepts.title: Mixed Quantum State
concepts.description: A quantum state whose density operator is not rank one, admitting statistical decompositions into pure states that need not be unique.

relations.note: Mixed states describe ensembles and reduced states of entangled systems.

concepts.title: Moment of Inertia
concepts.description: A measure of mass distribution relative to a specified rotation axis, given by mass weighted by squared perpendicular distance. General three-dimensional rigid-body rotation requires an inertia tensor; the scalar moment is its projection along the chosen axis.

concepts.title: Multiple Integral
concepts.description: An integral of a function over a region with two or more independent variables, accumulating values against an area or volume element; repeated one-dimensional integration is justified under appropriate integrability conditions.

relations.note: Riemann sums in several variables extend the single-variable construction used in this introduction.
Local coordinate definitions of form integrals use multivariable integration.

concepts.title: Natural Boundary Condition
concepts.description: A boundary condition derived by requiring boundary terms in the first variation to vanish for permitted endpoint variations, rather than prescribing those boundary values in advance.

relations.note: Allowing endpoint variations retains boundary contributions.
Natural conditions supplement the interior Euler-Lagrange equation when boundary values are free.

concepts.title: Navier–Stokes Equations
concepts.description: Continuum momentum-balance equations for Newtonian viscous fluids. The incompressible constant-property form couples velocity and pressure through pressure forces, viscous stress and body forces.

concepts.title: Newtonian Gravitation
concepts.description: The classical theory of gravitational attraction in which point masses exert an attractive inverse-square force on each other, with forces superposed for distributions of matter. It is distinct from the relativistic account of gravity as spacetime geometry.

relations.note: The isolated Newtonian two-body interaction produces Keplerian relative orbits.
A fixed point source is an important attractive inverse-square central force.

concepts.title: Newtonian Mechanics
concepts.description: The force-based formulation of classical mechanics, using Newton's laws to relate interactions, inertia, and the motion of particles or systems of particles in a specified reference frame.

relations.note: A formulation of classical dynamics, alongside the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations; this is not a special-case taxonomy edge.

concepts.title: Newton's Second Law
concepts.description: The dynamical law relating the net force on a material system to its momentum change. For a fixed-mass Newtonian particle in an inertial frame, the net force equals its mass times its acceleration.

concepts.title: Noether's Theorem
concepts.description: Noether's first theorem associates differentiable continuous variational symmetries with quantities conserved along Euler-Lagrange solutions, including symmetries of the Lagrangian up to a total derivative.

relations.note: The conservation law holds along solutions of the variational equations.
The relevant symmetry preserves the variational action, allowing boundary terms.
Continuous symmetries reveal conserved mechanical quantities.
The field-theoretic version relates global continuous variational symmetries to conserved currents; gauge redundancy needs separate care.

concepts.title: Normal Mode
concepts.description: A collective motion of a linearized coupled system in which the degrees of freedom keep a fixed relative pattern. For an undamped conservative system near stable equilibrium, each oscillatory mode has one frequency obtained from a mass-and-stiffness eigenvalue problem.

relations.note: Mode decomposition resolves small coupled oscillations into independent coordinates.

concepts.title: Normal Ordering
concepts.description: A reference-vacuum prescription that places quantum creation operators to the left of annihilation operators, including fermionic permutation signs when applicable.

concepts.title: Normal Subgroup
concepts.description: A subgroup preserved by conjugation with every element of its ambient group. Normality is a property relative to that ambient group.

relations.note: The kernel of a group homomorphism is a normal subgroup of its domain.

concepts.title: Open Quantum System
concepts.description: A quantum subsystem that interacts with an environment, so its reduced state need not evolve unitarily even when the combined system does.

concepts.title: Optical Path Length
concepts.description: The geometric length along an optical path weighted by the refractive index encountered. In a sequence of uniform media it is the sum of each segment length times its index; it is useful for comparing accumulated optical phase.

relations.note: The weighting of each geometric segment is the phase refractive index.
Differences in optical path contribute to the relative phase of recombined light.

concepts.title: Optical Theorem
concepts.description: A consequence of flux conservation that relates the total cross section to the imaginary part of the forward elastic scattering amplitude.

relations.note: The theorem uses the imaginary part of the forward elastic amplitude.
Its left side includes the total flux removed from the incident channel.

concepts.title: Optics
concepts.description: The study of light, its propagation and interaction with matter, and the instruments that form, guide or detect it. This introductory branch develops classical ray and wave descriptions.

concepts.title: Ordinary Differential Equation
concepts.description: An equation relating unknown functions of one independent variable to their derivatives with respect to that variable. It may be scalar or a system, linear or nonlinear, and is a shared mathematical construction rather than a physics-specific law.

relations.note: Equations of motion for finitely many mechanical degrees of freedom commonly form ODE systems.

concepts.title: Oscillation
concepts.description: Repeated variation of a dynamical quantity about a reference state or between extrema. Oscillations may be linear or nonlinear, free or driven, and need not remain exactly periodic when dissipation changes their amplitude.

concepts.title: Parallel Transport
concepts.description: A connection-dependent rule for moving tangent vectors along a curve while their covariant derivative along that curve vanishes.

concepts.title: Partial Derivative
concepts.description: The ordinary derivative of a multivariable function with respect to one coordinate while the other coordinates are fixed, evaluated wherever that derivative exists.

relations.note: Coordinate formulas differentiate coefficient functions with respect to individual coordinates.

concepts.title: Partial Differential Equation
concepts.description: An equation involving an unknown function of two or more independent variables and its partial derivatives. PDEs may be linear or nonlinear, occur in coupled systems, and require specified domains and data for particular solution problems.

relations.note: Local field equations commonly involve spacetime partial derivatives.
In coordinates, the field equations constrain metric and matter fields through a coupled system of partial differential equations.
Position-representation evolution with a local differential Hamiltonian is a PDE; abstract Hilbert-space evolution need not be.

concepts.title: Particle in a Box
concepts.description: An exactly solvable quantum model with a free particle inside a bounded region and impenetrable walls, producing discrete energies through boundary conditions.

relations.note: The hard-wall boundary conditions discretize stationary Schrödinger solutions.

concepts.title: Partition Function
concepts.description: A statistical-mechanical normalization sum or integral over weighted microscopic states; in the canonical ensemble, Z sums exp(−E/kBT) and determines equilibrium thermodynamic quantities.

relations.note: The canonical partition function normalizes Boltzmann weights.
Canonical mean energy follows from a derivative of log Z.
Canonical equilibrium entropy follows from Z and its temperature dependence.

concepts.title: Path Integral Formulation
concepts.description: A quantum formulation using appropriately defined or regulated sums over histories, with oscillatory action weights exp(i S / hbar) in real time, extending from particle paths to field configurations.

relations.note: Mechanical action provides the introductory particle-path construction.
Field-theory versions integrate over field histories and require a suitable definition or regulator.

concepts.title: Pauli Exclusion Principle
concepts.description: Identical fermions cannot occupy the same complete one-particle quantum state. For atomic electrons, opposite spin projections allow at most two electrons in a given spatial orbital.

relations.note: Exclusion concerns identical occupation of a complete one-particle state.
It limits the allowed atomic orbital occupancies.

concepts.title: Phase Space
concepts.description: A space whose points specify instantaneous states of a dynamical system. In finite-dimensional Hamiltonian mechanics its local coordinates include both generalized positions and conjugate momenta, unlike configuration space, which records configurations alone.

relations.note: Classical microscopic states and ensembles may be represented on phase space.

concepts.title: Phase Transition
concepts.description: A change between macroscopic phases, characterized in equilibrium theory by nonanalytic thermodynamic behavior in the appropriate infinite-system limit. Suitable order parameters distinguish many conventional phases, but no local order parameter describes every transition.

relations.note: Equilibrium phase comparisons use thermodynamic equilibrium states.
Sharp thermodynamic singularities arise in the infinite-system limit for ordinary equilibrium models.
Bose–Einstein condensation is an example of an equilibrium phase transition.

concepts.title: Phonon
concepts.description: A quantum of a collective vibrational normal mode of matter, described in a harmonic crystal as a bosonic lattice excitation.

relations.note: Harmonic lattice normal modes are quantized as independent quantum oscillators.
Thermal phonon populations account for the vibrational contribution to a solid's heat capacity.

concepts.title: Photon
concepts.description: The massless, electrically neutral quantum of the electromagnetic field; a physical free photon in vacuum has two transverse helicity states.

concepts.title: Planck's Law
concepts.description: The law giving the equilibrium black-body electromagnetic spectrum as a function of temperature and frequency or wavelength.

relations.note: The law describes the ideal equilibrium black-body spectrum.
Bosonic photon occupations with zero chemical potential, multiplied by electromagnetic mode density, yield the law.

concepts.title: Poincaré Group
concepts.description: The isometry group of four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, combining spacetime translations with Lorentz transformations through a semidirect-product group law.

relations.note: The origin-preserving subgroup supplies the Lorentz part of each affine isometry.
Translations and Lorentz transformations form flat-spacetime kinematical symmetries.
Relativistic fields and particle states carry suitable representations of Poincaré symmetry.

concepts.title: Poincaré Lemma
concepts.description: The result that every closed differential form of positive degree is locally exact on a smooth manifold, with global exactness on star-shaped open subsets of Euclidean space.

relations.note: It gives vanishing positive-degree de Rham cohomology on star-shaped domains.

concepts.title: Poisson Bracket
concepts.description: A bilinear, antisymmetric operation on classical observables that obeys the Leibniz and Jacobi identities. In canonical phase coordinates it is built from paired position and momentum derivatives and describes Hamiltonian evolution and generators of transformations.

concepts.title: Polarization
concepts.description: The pattern traced by a transverse light wave's electric-field direction as it oscillates. Linear polarization keeps that direction along a fixed transverse axis; circular and elliptical polarization rotate it.

relations.note: Optical polarization specifies the transverse electric-field oscillation.
The field's orientation matters when light passes through an analyzer or when polarized waves interfere.

concepts.title: Position
concepts.description: The location of a point relative to a chosen spatial reference system. In Euclidean mechanics, a chosen origin identifies that location with a position vector, whose coordinates may depend on time.

relations.note: After choosing an origin, the elementary Euclidean representation describes position with a geometric vector.

concepts.title: Potential Energy
concepts.description: Energy assigned to a configuration for conservative mechanical interactions, with differences fixed by minus the work of the conservative force. The reference value is arbitrary, while the spatial variation determines that force.

relations.note: For standard velocity-independent conservative interactions, the Lagrangian includes minus the potential energy.
For standard time-independent Cartesian particle models, the Hamiltonian is the sum of kinetic and potential energies.

concepts.title: Pressure
concepts.description: The scalar intensity of isotropic compressive contact force. In a fluid at rest, pressure gives normal force per unit area and is the same for every surface orientation at a point.

concepts.title: Principal Quantum Number
concepts.description: The positive integer n that labels an atomic electron shell. In the nonrelativistic one-electron Coulomb problem it also labels the energy level, while multi-electron orbital energies need additional information.

relations.note: The Coulomb bound levels are indexed by n.
Atomic configuration notation includes the occupied shell index.

concepts.title: Principle of Relativity
concepts.description: The requirement that the laws of physics take the same form in all inertial frames; together with light-speed invariance it motivates special relativity.

concepts.title: Probability Amplitude
concepts.description: A complex quantity whose squared magnitude gives an outcome probability, with relative phases controlling interference between indistinguishable alternatives.

concepts.title: Probability Current
concepts.description: A vector field describing local transport of probability and balancing changes in probability density through a continuity equation.

concepts.title: Probability Distribution
concepts.description: A probability measure specifying how total probability is assigned to possible outcomes or values of a random variable. Discrete laws may be represented by probability masses; only laws with a density admit a probability-density representation.

relations.note: A distribution obeys the axioms of probability.
An ensemble assigns probabilities to microscopic states under specified macroscopic conditions.

concepts.title: Probability Theory
concepts.description: The mathematical study of uncertainty using probability spaces, random variables, distributions, and their relationships. It provides a framework for assigning consistent probabilities to events and analyzing random phenomena.

relations.note: Probabilities describe microscopic states, ensemble averages, and fluctuations.
Probability is a supporting mathematical framework for physical models with uncertainty or many microscopic possibilities.

concepts.title: Propagator
concepts.description: In quantum field theory, a two-point field correlation or Green function with specified ordering and boundary conditions; the Feynman propagator uses time ordering and appears in perturbative diagrams.

relations.note: Internal lines represent propagator factors according to the chosen theory and convention.

concepts.title: Proper Time
concepts.description: Elapsed time recorded by an ideal clock along a timelike worldline, obtained by integrating its Lorentzian interval; it cannot parameterize a null worldline.

relations.note: Proper time is an affine parameter on timelike Levi-Civita geodesics, but not on null geodesics.

concepts.title: Pseudo-Riemannian Manifold
concepts.description: A smooth manifold equipped with a nondegenerate symmetric metric tensor of arbitrary signature, encompassing both Riemannian and Lorentzian geometries.

relations.note: Riemannian manifolds are the positive-definite-signature special case.
Lorentzian manifolds are the one-timelike-direction signature special case.

concepts.title: Pullback of Differential Forms
concepts.description: For a smooth map f from M to N, the operation sending a differential k-form on N to a k-form on M by applying the differential of f to each tangent-vector argument before evaluating the original form.

relations.note: Pullback commutes with exterior differentiation and induces maps on de Rham cohomology.

concepts.title: Pure Quantum State
concepts.description: A quantum state represented by a rank-one density operator, equivalently by a unit vector in a complex Hilbert space up to an overall phase.

concepts.title: Quantum Angular Momentum
concepts.description: Angular momentum represented by quantum observables whose Cartesian components obey a noncommuting rotation algebra. It includes orbital, intrinsic-spin and total angular momentum.

relations.note: Angular momentum components are measurable quantities represented by self-adjoint operators.
Commuting angular momentum observables separate and label the central Coulomb eigenproblem.

concepts.title: Quantum Decoherence
concepts.description: Suppression of locally observable quantum interference as a system becomes correlated with unobserved environmental degrees of freedom.

concepts.title: Quantum Dynamics
concepts.description: The study of how quantum states, observables, and transition probabilities change with time.

concepts.title: Quantum Electrodynamics
concepts.description: The relativistic quantum field theory of electromagnetic interactions, coupling charged matter to the quantized electromagnetic field through local U(1) gauge symmetry.

concepts.title: Quantum Entanglement
concepts.description: For finite-dimensional composite systems, the property of a joint state that cannot be written as a convex combination of product states of the subsystems; for a pure state this reduces to failure to factor as one product vector.

relations.note: Entanglement expresses correlations not obtainable by a statistical mixture of independent local states.

concepts.title: Quantum Field
concepts.description: A spacetime-indexed operator-valued distribution whose smearing with suitable test functions gives operators on quantum states, rather than an ordinary classical field value at each point.

concepts.title: Quantum Field Theory
concepts.description: The quantum framework for local field degrees of freedom and their interactions, used in relativistic physics and many-body systems; this introductory branch emphasizes relativistic theories.

relations.note: Classical actions and fields organize the introductory quantization route.
Lorentz symmetry is a prerequisite for the relativistic emphasis here, not for every many-body quantum field theory.

concepts.title: Quantum Hamiltonian
concepts.description: A self-adjoint energy operator generating quantum time evolution under the appropriate domain and evolution assumptions, distinct from the classical Hamiltonian function on phase space.

concepts.title: Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
concepts.description: The quantum model of a particle in a quadratic confining potential, with equally spaced energy levels and a nonzero ground-state energy.

relations.note: The energy operator combines kinetic energy with a positive quadratic potential.
Normalizable stationary solutions determine the oscillator spectrum.

concepts.title: Quantum Mechanics
concepts.description: The framework describing quantum states, observables, probabilities, and dynamics, with linear operators on complex vector spaces as its central mathematical structure.

concepts.title: Quantum Observable
concepts.description: A measurable quantity represented, for a sharp measurement in the standard Hilbert-space formalism, by a self-adjoint operator whose spectral measure determines the possible outcomes.

relations.note: The quantum Hamiltonian is the energy observable that generates time evolution.

concepts.title: Quantum Perturbation Theory
concepts.description: Approximation methods that expand quantum energies, states, or transition amplitudes around a solvable Hamiltonian when the added interaction is sufficiently weak.

relations.note: The calculation separates an unperturbed energy operator from a small added interaction.
Expanding the stationary Schrödinger eigenproblem gives successive energy and state corrections.

concepts.title: Quantum Scattering
concepts.description: The study of how incident quantum states are transformed by interactions, using outgoing amplitudes and cross sections to characterize the target and interaction.

relations.note: Nonrelativistic potential-scattering states solve the stationary Schrödinger problem.

concepts.title: Quantum State
concepts.description: A specification of quantum measurement probabilities, represented in the standard Hilbert-space formulation by a positive trace-class operator of trace one, including pure and mixed states.

relations.note: Pure states correspond to rank-one density operators.
Mixed states are density operators that are not pure.

concepts.title: Quantum Statistical Mechanics
concepts.description: The statistical description of quantum many-particle systems, using quantum ensembles and density operators to connect microscopic states with thermal behavior.

relations.note: A density matrix represents the statistical quantum state.
Quantum thermal descriptions specify ensembles of microscopic states.

concepts.title: Quantum Superposition
concepts.description: The formation of a pure quantum state from a nonzero complex linear combination of state vectors followed by normalization, retaining relative phases rather than mixing classical probabilities.

concepts.title: Quantum Tunnelling
concepts.description: Quantum transmission through a potential barrier that would forbid passage by a classical particle with the same total energy.

relations.note: The wave amplitude extends into the classically forbidden barrier region.
Matching stationary Schrödinger solutions gives a nonzero transmitted component.

concepts.title: Quantum Variational Method
concepts.description: A method that estimates a quantum ground-state energy by minimizing the Hamiltonian expectation value over an admissible family of trial states.

relations.note: The Hamiltonian defines the trial state's energy functional.
A trial family can approximate a normalizable ground-state eigenfunction.

concepts.title: Quantum Zeno Effect
concepts.description: Inhibition of transitions by sufficiently frequent suitable measurements or measurement-like interactions.

concepts.title: Quotient Group
concepts.description: The group of cosets of a normal subgroup, with multiplication induced by the original group operation. Normality makes the coset operation well-defined.

relations.note: The natural quotient map is surjective and has the chosen normal subgroup as its kernel.

concepts.title: Rabi Oscillation
concepts.description: Coherent oscillation of occupation probabilities between coupled quantum levels, typically driven by a near-resonant field.

concepts.title: Random Variable
concepts.description: A measurable function on a probability space that assigns a numerical value to each possible outcome. Its distribution records the probabilities of its possible values or ranges of values.

relations.note: A random variable is defined on a probability space.
Classical observables such as energy can be treated as random variables on an ensemble of microstates.

concepts.title: Cosmological Recombination
concepts.description: The formation of neutral atoms from ions and electrons as the expanding early universe cooled, reducing free electrons and helping photons decouple.

relations.note: Hydrogen binding energies and atomic states enter recombination.
The falling free-electron abundance influences photon last scattering.
Atomic recombination forms part of the thermal history of the universe.

concepts.title: Rectangular Potential Barrier
concepts.description: A piecewise-constant quantum potential model with a finite region raised above the exterior potential, used to calculate reflection and transmission.

relations.note: The piecewise potential defines the particle's energy operator.
Exact matching predicts transmission even when the energy lies below the barrier.

concepts.title: Reduced Mass
concepts.description: The effective inertial parameter multiplying relative acceleration in the separated Newtonian two-body problem. For two positive masses it is their product divided by their sum, and approaches the lighter mass when the other mass becomes much larger.

concepts.title: Refraction
concepts.description: A change in a light ray's direction as it propagates through regions with different optical properties. At an ordinary boundary this is associated with a change in phase speed; normal incidence need not change the direction.

relations.note: Refraction redirects transmitted rays in optical ray models.

concepts.title: Refractive Index
concepts.description: A dimensionless measure of optical phase propagation: in the present transparent, isotropic-medium scope, it is the speed of light in vacuum divided by the phase speed in the medium at a specified frequency.

relations.note: The index specifies ray refraction and optical path in a material.

concepts.title: Relativity
concepts.description: The family of physical theories relating spacetime, motion, and reference frames, including special relativity and the general-relativistic description of gravitation.

relations.note: Relativity begins by distinguishing coordinate descriptions from observer-independent physical laws.

concepts.title: Relativity of Simultaneity
concepts.description: Spatially separated events judged simultaneous in one inertial frame need not be simultaneous in another frame moving relative to it.

concepts.title: Resonance
concepts.description: An enhanced response when a system is driven near a characteristic frequency. The location and width of a resonance depend on damping, the measured response, and the drive; displacement and power peaks need not occur at the same frequency.

relations.note: The linear driven oscillator supplies the introductory mechanical model; resonance also occurs in other systems.

concepts.title: Reynolds Number
concepts.description: A dimensionless comparison of characteristic inertial and viscous effects in a flow, formed from chosen velocity and length scales and the fluid's density and dynamic viscosity.

concepts.title: Ricci Curvature
concepts.description: A rank-two contraction of the Riemann curvature tensor; for a Levi-Civita connection it is symmetric, governs infinitesimal volume distortion, and enters Einstein's field equations.

relations.note: It is obtained by contracting one upper and one lower index of the Riemann tensor.

concepts.title: Riemann Curvature Tensor
concepts.description: The tensor of an affine connection that measures the noncommutativity of covariant derivatives and the failure of the connection to be locally flat.

relations.note: In coordinates it is constructed from first derivatives and quadratic combinations of the connection coefficients.

concepts.title: Riemann Integral
concepts.description: For a bounded real function on a closed bounded interval, the common limit of tagged partition sums as the largest subinterval length tends to zero, when that limit exists independently of the tags.

concepts.title: Riemann Normal Coordinates
concepts.description: Coordinates constructed from the metric exponential map near a point, where Levi-Civita coefficients vanish at that point; curvature generally remains nonzero.

concepts.title: Riemannian Manifold
concepts.description: A smooth manifold equipped with a smoothly varying positive-definite metric tensor, defining lengths, angles, volumes, and geodesic distance.

concepts.title: Rigid Body
concepts.description: An idealized extended body for which the Euclidean distance between every pair of material points remains constant during motion. It can translate and rotate, while deformation and internal elastic modes are excluded.

concepts.title: Rotational Dynamics
concepts.description: The classical study of rotational motion and its changes under applied torques, using angular momentum and mass distribution. Rigid bodies are central models, but their motion need not remain about a single fixed axis.

relations.note: Instantaneous angular velocity describes the rotational motion whose changes are studied.
A standard prerequisite for the rigid-body models studied in rotational dynamics.

concepts.title: Rydberg Formula
concepts.description: The relation expressing hydrogen spectral-line wavenumbers as differences of inverse squared principal quantum numbers.

relations.note: The hydrogen form follows from Bohr energies and the photon energy–frequency relation.
It predicts leading wavelengths within the hydrogen spectral series.

concepts.title: Cosmic Scale Factor
concepts.description: The time-dependent factor describing how physical separations of comoving points scale in a homogeneous cosmological background.

relations.note: The scale factor multiplies the spatial part of the FLRW metric.
Ratios of scale factors determine the cosmological redshift of freely propagating light.

concepts.title: Scattering Amplitude
concepts.description: The complex coefficient of an outgoing scattered wave relative to the incident wave, encoding angular strength and phase in a chosen normalization.

relations.note: The amplitude is defined by the scattering wavefunction's far-field asymptotic form.
Its modulus squared gives the differential cross section for the scoped elastic normalization.

concepts.title: Scattering Cross Section
concepts.description: An effective area that relates incident particle flux to a scattering rate; its differential form resolves the outgoing direction or other final-state variables.

relations.note: Cross sections quantify measurable scattering rates and angular distributions.

concepts.title: Scattering Matrix
concepts.description: The operator or matrix that relates asymptotic incoming quantum channels to outgoing channels and encodes their transition amplitudes.

relations.note: Incoming and outgoing asymptotic wave solutions define its channels.
The channel matrix organizes the possible scattering outcomes.

concepts.title: Schrödinger Equation
concepts.description: The evolution equation i hbar d|psi>/dt = H(t)|psi> for a closed quantum system's state vector, with H the Hamiltonian operator and suitable domain conditions.

relations.note: A self-adjoint Hamiltonian gives unitary dynamics under the appropriate evolution hypotheses.
The Hamiltonian operator specifies the equation's generator.

concepts.title: Schrödinger Picture
concepts.description: A representation that assigns Hamiltonian-generated time evolution to state vectors while observable operators retain only any explicit time dependence.

concepts.title: Schwarzschild Coordinates
concepts.description: Coordinates (t, r, θ, φ) displaying Schwarzschild symmetry, with r an areal radius; the usual chart is singular at the black-hole horizon.

concepts.title: Schwarzschild Radius
concepts.description: The length r_s = 2GM/c² associated with a mass M; it is the horizon's areal radius for the Schwarzschild black-hole solution, not for every material body.

relations.note: Its horizon interpretation applies to the Schwarzschild black-hole geometry.

concepts.title: Schwarzschild Spacetime
concepts.description: The static, spherically symmetric vacuum spacetime outside an uncharged, non-rotating gravitating mass, represented by the Schwarzschild solution of general relativity.

concepts.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics
concepts.description: The thermodynamic law that total entropy cannot decrease in an isolated system, restricting process direction beyond energy conservation.

relations.note: The entropy formulation quantifies irreversibility.
It constrains equilibrium and energy conversion.

concepts.title: Second Variation
concepts.description: The second-order variation of a sufficiently smooth functional under admissible perturbations, represented by a quadratic form that helps distinguish minima from other stationary points.

relations.note: Second-order analysis follows the first-order stationarity test.
Nonnegative second variation is necessary for a local minimum under standard smoothness assumptions.

concepts.title: Self-adjoint Operator
concepts.description: A densely defined linear operator on a Hilbert space equal to its adjoint in both action and domain; in finite dimensions this is a Hermitian matrix in an orthonormal basis.

relations.note: The standard sharp-observable formalism uses self-adjoint operators.

concepts.title: Simple Harmonic Oscillator
concepts.description: An undriven, undamped dynamical model with a linear restoring force proportional to displacement from a stable equilibrium. Its nonzero motions are sinusoidal with an amplitude-independent frequency.

relations.note: The introductory mechanical restoring-force model relates the net force to acceleration.
For a constant mass acted on by a linear restoring force.
Each positive-frequency undamped linear normal coordinate obeys an independent harmonic-oscillator equation.
Approximates planar pendulum librations only at small angular amplitude.

concepts.title: Simple Pendulum
concepts.description: An ideal point mass constrained at a fixed distance from a pivot in a uniform gravitational field. For planar motion without friction its angular equation is nonlinear; only small oscillations about the downward equilibrium are approximately harmonic.

relations.note: The introductory mechanical model uses tangential force balance to determine angular acceleration.
The tangential force equation gives the planar angular dynamics.

concepts.title: Smooth Atlas
concepts.description: A covering collection of coordinate charts whose overlap transitions are infinitely differentiable, specifying a smooth structure after maximal extension.

concepts.title: Smooth Manifold
concepts.description: A topological manifold equipped with a compatible smooth atlas, making differentiation of functions, curves, and maps well-defined across coordinate charts.

relations.note: Forgetting the chosen nondegenerate metric leaves a smooth manifold.
A maximal smooth atlas specifies the smooth structure.
Forgetting the holomorphic structure leaves an underlying real smooth manifold; this does not assert that every smooth manifold admits a complex structure.
Forgetting the chosen symplectic form leaves a smooth manifold; this does not assert that every smooth manifold admits such a form.

concepts.title: Smooth Map
concepts.description: A map between smooth manifolds whose local expressions in compatible coordinates are infinitely differentiable.

relations.note: Diffeomorphisms additionally have smooth inverses.

concepts.title: Snell's Law
concepts.description: The relation between the incident and transmitted ray angles at a boundary between two isotropic optical media: each refractive index multiplies the sine of the corresponding angle to the normal.

relations.note: The indices of the two media are the material inputs to this law.
The law quantifies the incident and refracted ray geometry.
Ray tracing applies this law at refracting boundaries.

concepts.title: Solid Mechanics
concepts.description: The study of forces, motion and deformation in solid materials, including elastic and irreversible responses within continuum models.

concepts.title: Solid-State Physics
concepts.description: The study of physical properties of solids and their microscopic origins, including electronic states and collective lattice behavior.

relations.note: The microscopic band and phonon description develops quantum mechanics in solids.

concepts.title: Spacetime Interval
concepts.description: In Minkowski spacetime, the invariant squared separation of two events, -c²Δt² + Δx² + Δy² + Δz² in the mostly-plus convention.

concepts.title: Special Relativity
concepts.description: The theory of space and time for inertial physics without gravitation, built on Lorentz invariance and a frame-independent speed of light.

concepts.title: Special Unitary Group
concepts.description: The matrix Lie group SU(n) consisting of complex n-by-n unitary matrices with determinant one, with matrix multiplication as its group operation.

relations.note: SU(n) is a compact matrix Lie group.
Its defining matrices preserve the standard Hermitian inner product.
SU(2), the double cover of spatial rotations, organizes spin angular-momentum representations.
The fundamental SU(2) action rotates a two-component state after an overall phase is removed.

concepts.title: Spectral Line
concepts.description: A localized excess or deficit of intensity over a narrow frequency range in a radiation spectrum. Atomic and molecular emission or absorption transitions produce characteristic lines.

relations.note: Measured line frequencies reveal atomic internal transitions.

concepts.title: Spin Angular Momentum
concepts.description: Intrinsic quantum angular momentum carried by particles, independent of orbital motion. A particle's spin quantum number fixes its allowed magnitude and projection values; an electron has spin one-half.

relations.note: Spin observables obey the angular momentum algebra.
Electronic spin contributes to the atom's magnetic interaction.

concepts.title: Spin–Statistics Theorem
concepts.description: The relativistic result connecting integer spin with bosonic exchange symmetry and half-integer spin with fermionic exchange antisymmetry, under locality and positivity assumptions.

concepts.title: Spinor
concepts.description: An element of a spin representation associated with a quadratic space; rotations act through a spin double cover, and a continuously lifted full turn changes a spinor's sign.

relations.note: Spinors transform in representations of spin groups rather than ordinary vector representations of the rotation group.
Clifford modules give a construction of spin representations.
Two-component spinors carry the spin-one-half rotation representation.
Dirac and Weyl fields have spinor-valued components with relativistic transformation laws.

concepts.title: Stark Effect
concepts.description: The displacement or splitting of atomic or molecular spectral lines when an applied electric field changes the energy levels. The response can be linear or quadratic in the field, depending on the states and their degeneracies.

relations.note: An external electric field is the perturbation defining the effect.
The model describes the shift by adding an electric interaction to the atomic Hamiltonian.

concepts.title: Stationary State
concepts.description: A pure energy eigenstate of a time-independent Hamiltonian whose evolution changes only an overall phase, leaving time-independent observable statistics unchanged.

concepts.title: Statistical Ensemble
concepts.description: A probability distribution over possible microscopic states of a system, used to calculate averages and fluctuations subject to specified macroscopic conditions.

relations.note: Probabilities are assigned to microscopic states.
Fixed-energy equilibrium gives the microcanonical ensemble.
Thermal-reservoir equilibrium gives the canonical ensemble.
The ensemble specifies a probability law over microscopic states.

concepts.title: Statistical Mechanics
concepts.description: The probabilistic description of many-body systems that connects microscopic dynamics and states to macroscopic properties, including equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuations.

relations.note: Ensembles encode microscopic probabilities.
Macroscopic observables connect the two descriptions.
Equilibrium statistics supplies microscopic models of thermodynamic behavior.

concepts.title: Stokes' Theorem
concepts.description: For an oriented smooth n-manifold M with boundary and a compactly supported smooth (n-1)-form omega, the integral of d omega over M equals the integral of the boundary pullback of omega with the induced boundary orientation.

relations.note: On an oriented interval, Stokes' theorem recovers endpoint evaluation of the integral of a derivative.

concepts.title: Stress–Energy Tensor
concepts.description: A tensor encoding local energy density, momentum density, energy flux and stresses; the symmetric matter tensor supplies the source term in Einstein's equations.

relations.note: Field theories encode energy and momentum in stress-energy tensors.

concepts.title: Subgroup
concepts.description: A subset of a group containing its identity and closed under the inherited multiplication and inverses, so that it is itself a group.

relations.note: The operation is inherited from an ambient group.
Kernels and images are subgroups.

concepts.title: Submanifold
concepts.description: In this record, an embedded smooth submanifold is a subset of a smooth manifold that is locally a coordinate plane in suitable ambient charts, with the induced topology and smooth structure.

concepts.title: Symplectic Manifold
concepts.description: A smooth manifold equipped with a closed differential 2-form that is nondegenerate at every point, necessarily giving the manifold even dimension.

relations.note: Symplectic forms determine the geometric form of Hamiltonian evolution.

concepts.title: Tangent Space
concepts.description: The vector space at a point of a smooth manifold whose elements represent tangent directions, equivalently velocities of curves or derivations at that point.

relations.note: A tangent space is a vector space of directions at a point.

concepts.title: Taylor Series
concepts.description: The power series about a point whose coefficients are the function's successive derivatives there divided by factorials; an infinitely differentiable function need not equal this series.

relations.note: Taylor polynomials and remainder estimates support local approximation.

concepts.title: Temperature
concepts.description: An intensive thermodynamic variable characterizing thermal equilibrium; its absolute scale relates reversible heat transfer to entropy change.

relations.note: Thermal equilibrium underpins temperature comparison.
Reservoir temperature controls equilibrium probabilities.

concepts.title: Tensor Field
concepts.description: A smooth assignment of a multilinear tensor, built from tangent and cotangent spaces, to every point of a smooth manifold.

relations.note: Differential k-forms are alternating covariant tensor fields of rank k.
A metric is a nondegenerate symmetric covariant rank-two tensor field.

concepts.title: Tensor Product
concepts.description: A vector space generated by pairs of vectors from two spaces over the same scalar field, subject to bilinearity, so bilinear maps from the pair factor uniquely through a linear map from the tensor product.

relations.note: The construction starts from two vector spaces over the same field.
Composite-state spaces allow sums of product vectors that do not factor into one product.
Adding angular momenta of two spins uses operators on their tensor-product space.

concepts.title: Thermal Equilibrium
concepts.description: A relation between systems that exhibit no net heat transfer when placed in thermal contact under otherwise fixed constraints.

relations.note: Equilibrium classes underpin empirical temperature.
The system equilibrates with a thermal reservoir.

concepts.title: Thermodynamic Entropy
concepts.description: An equilibrium state function satisfying dS = δQrev/T along a reversible path, whose total change is nonnegative for an isolated system.

relations.note: Absolute temperature relates reversible heat to entropy.
Entropy expresses the direction of allowed processes.
Macroscopic entropy is related to microscopic state statistics.

concepts.title: Thermodynamic Limit
concepts.description: The limit of an increasingly large system while intensive controls such as particle density are held fixed, used to define bulk thermodynamics.

relations.note: The bulk construction is a controlled limiting process.
Thermodynamic singularities can emerge when the number of degrees of freedom becomes infinite.

concepts.title: Thermodynamic Process
concepts.description: A change of a system's thermodynamic state under specified interactions or constraints; intermediate states need not remain in equilibrium.

relations.note: A working substance follows a repeatable cycle of processes to deliver net work.

concepts.title: Thermodynamics
concepts.description: The macroscopic study of energy transfer, equilibrium, and constraints on physical processes, using thermodynamic laws without resolving individual microscopic states.

relations.note: Equilibrium gives the reference states.
Energy accounting is fundamental.
Entropy constrains possible processes.

concepts.title: Thin Lens
concepts.description: A lens model in which the separation of the two refracting surfaces can be neglected for image formation. For rays close to the optical axis, it relates object position, image position and focal length.

relations.note: A refracting lens forms an image by redirecting transmitted rays.
The approximation reduces lens image formation to ray geometry and focal length.

concepts.title: Tight-Binding Approximation
concepts.description: A quantum model using localized orbitals and hopping between sites to approximate electronic states in a solid or lattice.

relations.note: On-site and hopping matrix elements define the model Hamiltonian.
Localized orbitals motivate the basis for conventional electronic tight binding.
Diagonalizing a periodic tight-binding Hamiltonian gives approximate energy bands.

concepts.title: Time Dilation
concepts.description: In special relativity, elapsed coordinate time in an inertial frame exceeds a moving clock's proper time; at constant speed, Δt = γ Δτ.

concepts.title: Torque
concepts.description: The moment of a force about a specified reference point, obtained from the lever-arm vector crossed with the force. Torques from different applied forces add; torque is not a force and its value generally depends on the reference point.

relations.note: In oriented three-dimensional Euclidean space, torque is the lever-arm vector crossed with the force.

concepts.title: Total Internal Reflection
concepts.description: At an ideal lossless boundary, light incident from the higher-index medium above the critical angle has no propagating transmitted ray and its power is reflected back. An evanescent field can still extend into the lower-index medium.

relations.note: The critical angle follows when the refracted angle reaches ninety degrees.
It bounds which rays can leave a high-index optical element.

concepts.title: Two-Body Problem
concepts.description: Determining the motion of two mutually interacting bodies. In Newtonian mechanics, an isolated pair with equal-and-opposite internal forces separates into center-of-mass motion and relative motion governed by the reduced mass; an additional central-force assumption permits the usual orbital reduction.

relations.note: The separated equations follow by summing and subtracting the two particle equations with equal-and-opposite internal forces.
An isolated attractive inverse-square two-body interaction reduces to a Kepler problem for the relative coordinate.

concepts.title: Two-state Quantum System
concepts.description: A quantum system with a two-dimensional state space, allowing arbitrary superpositions and mixtures of two independent basis states.

concepts.title: Uncertainty Principle
concepts.description: A constraint on statistical spreads of quantum observables in a given state. The Robertson bound relates the product of their standard deviations to the expectation value of their commutator, subject to the relevant operator-domain conditions.

concepts.title: Unitary Operator
concepts.description: A surjective linear operator on a complex Hilbert space that preserves inner products, equivalently a bounded operator whose adjoint is its inverse.

relations.note: A unitary operator is a linear map acting on one Hilbert space.
The defining preservation law uses the Hilbert inner product and adjoint.
Unitary conjugation relates Schrödinger and Heisenberg observables.
Unitary basis changes and closed-system dynamics preserve state norms and transition probabilities.

concepts.title: Quantum Vacuum State
concepts.description: A lowest-energy state of a quantum field theory for the chosen time evolution; a free-field vacuum has no particle excitations but can have nonzero field correlations.

concepts.title: Variance
concepts.description: For a real random variable with a finite mean, the expected squared deviation from that mean. A finite second moment gives Var(X) = E[X²] − E[X]²; if the second moment diverges, the variance need not be finite.

relations.note: Variance is an expectation of squared deviations from the mean.
Variance quantifies the spread of a real random variable.
Variances measure equilibrium fluctuations, including energy fluctuations in a canonical ensemble.

concepts.title: Variational Principle
concepts.description: A formulation in which physical configurations or trajectories are characterized as stationary points of a functional, especially the action in mechanics and field theory.

relations.note: Stationarity is expressed by vanishing admissible first variations.
Stationary-function methods formulate physical models.

concepts.title: Vector Bundle
concepts.description: In this record, a smooth real vector bundle is a fixed-rank family of real vector spaces over a smooth manifold, with smooth local trivializations that act linearly on each fiber.

relations.note: Tensor fields are sections of tensor bundles.

concepts.title: Vector Field
concepts.description: An assignment of a Euclidean vector to each point of a region of ordinary three-dimensional space.

relations.note: Needed for the scoped vector field formulation.

concepts.title: Vector Space
concepts.description: A set equipped with vector addition and scalar multiplication over a field, satisfying the vector-space axioms so that linear combinations are defined.

relations.note: An inner product adds positive-definite geometric structure to a real or complex vector space.

concepts.title: Velocity
concepts.description: The instantaneous rate of change of position with respect to time in a specified reference frame. It is a vector; its magnitude is speed and its direction is tangent to a differentiable trajectory when the velocity is nonzero.

concepts.title: Velocity Field
concepts.description: A vector field assigning the bulk velocity of a material element to its current position and time in a continuum.

relations.note: This node specifically uses the Eulerian description.

concepts.title: Wave Optics
concepts.description: The classical description of light that retains its wave amplitude, phase and polarization to explain interference, diffraction and related effects.

concepts.title: Wavefunction
concepts.description: A complex probability-amplitude representation of a pure quantum state, commonly as a function of configuration coordinates, with additional components when spin or other internal degrees of freedom are present.

relations.note: Wave mechanics expresses state evolution through the wavefunction.

concepts.title: Wedge Product
concepts.description: The exterior multiplication operation on differential forms, combining a p-form and a q-form into a form of degree p+q. Its sign changes according to the degrees when the factors are exchanged.

concepts.title: Wick's Theorem
concepts.description: An identity that rewrites time-ordered free-field products as normal-ordered products and pair contractions, enabling perturbative quantum-field calculations.

concepts.title: WKB Approximation
concepts.description: A semiclassical approximation that exploits slow spatial variation of the local wavelength to estimate quantum wavefunctions, quantization, and barrier transmission.

relations.note: Neglecting sufficiently small spatial-variation terms gives the semiclassical solution.
The forbidden-region solution estimates exponentially suppressed barrier transmission.

concepts.title: Work
concepts.description: Mechanical energy transfer associated with a force acting through displacement of its point of application. Along a trajectory, infinitesimal work is the scalar product of force and displacement, integrated over the motion.

relations.note: Displacement records the change in position of the force's point of application.
Parameterizing the trajectory converts work to an ordinary definite integral.
The Euclidean dot product selects the component of force along the displacement.
Mechanical work is one contribution to energy transfer across a thermodynamic system boundary.

concepts.title: Work–Energy Theorem
concepts.description: The statement that net work along a particle's actual trajectory equals its kinetic-energy change. In Newtonian mechanics it follows by integrating the scalar product of the equation of motion with displacement.

concepts.title: Zeeman Effect
concepts.description: The splitting of spectral lines in a static magnetic field through shifts of the underlying energy levels. Electronic orbital and spin magnetic moments contribute to the atomic effect.

relations.note: A static external magnetic field induces the energy changes.
The spectroscopic effect is resolved as splitting of transition lines.
